title.en: Volume 63 Biographies 28: Fan Zigai, Shi Xiang, Yuan Shou, Yang Yichen, Wei Xuan, Liu Quan
title.raw: 卷63 列傳第28 樊子蓋 史祥 元壽 楊義臣 衞玄 劉權 Volume 63 Biographies 28: Fan Zigai, Shi Xiang, Yuan Shou, Yang Yichen, Wei Xuan, Liu Quan

sentences.zh: 隋書卷六十三列傳第二十八

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 63, Biographies Twenty-Eight
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 63, Biographies Twenty-Eight

sentences.zh: ○樊子蓋

translations.literal: ○ Fan Zigai
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai

sentences.zh: 樊子蓋，字華宗，廬江人也。

translations.literal: Fan Zigai, style name Huazong, was a native of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigai, whose style name was Huazong, came from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 祖道則，梁越州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dao Ze was Inspector of Yue Province under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dao Ze had served as Inspector of Yue Province under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 父儒，侯景之亂奔于齊，官至仁州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ru, during the turmoil of Hou Jing, fled to Qi and rose to the post of Governor of Renzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ru fled to Northern Qi during Hou Jing's rebellion and eventually became governor of Renzhou.

sentences.zh: 子蓋解褐武興王行參軍，出為慎縣令，東汝、北陳二郡太守，員外散騎常侍，封富陽縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Zigai began his career as a staff officer to the Prince of Wuxing, then served as Magistrate of Shen County, as Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Dongru and Beichen, as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering service, Zigai became an aide to the Prince of Wuxing, then magistrate of Shen County, grand administrator of Dongru and Beichen, supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuyang with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，授儀同三司，治郢州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he was appointed Colonel in the Third Rank with ceremonial parity and Acting Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou conquered Qi, he was made a third-rank colonel with ceremonial parity and acting governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，以儀同領鄉兵，後除樅陽太守。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he led local militia in the capacity of a colonel with ceremonial parity, and was later appointed Grand Administrator of Zongyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen accepted the throne, he led local militia while holding the rank of ceremonial colonel, and was later appointed grand administrator of Zongyang.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以功加上開府，改封上蔡縣伯，食邑七百戶，賜物三千段，粟九千斛。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, for his merit he was promoted to Senior General with the Opening Office, his fief was changed to Baron of Shangcai with seven hundred households, and he was granted three thousand bolts of goods and nine thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen, his achievements earned him promotion to senior opening-office general, a change of fief to Baron of Shangcai with seven hundred households, and gifts of three thousand bolts of silk and nine thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 拜辰州刺史，俄轉嵩州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Chenzhou, and soon transferred to Governor of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Chenzhou and soon afterward transferred to governor of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned his post to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起授齊州刺史，固讓，不許。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled and appointed Governor of Qizhou; he firmly declined, but was not permitted to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was recalled and appointed governor of Qizhou; he declined firmly, but the court would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 其年，轉循州總管，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: That same year he was transferred to General-in-Chief of Xunzhou, with authorization to act at his own discretion.
translations.idiomatic: In that same year he was made general-in-chief of Xunzhou, with leave to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 十八年入朝，奏嶺南地圖，賜以良馬雜物，加統四州，令還任所，遣光祿少卿柳謇之餞於霸上。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he came to court, presented a map of Lingnan, and was granted fine horses and various goods; four more prefectures were added to his command, and he was ordered back to his post, with Vice Director of the Imperial Household Liu Jianzhi seeing him off at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he came to court and presented a map of the Lingnan region; the emperor bestowed fine horses and assorted gifts, added four prefectures to his jurisdiction, and ordered him back to his post, with Vice Director of the Imperial Household Liu Jianzhi seeing him off at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，征還京師，轉涼州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he was summoned back to the capital and transferred to Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Zigai was recalled to the capital and transferred to governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子蓋言於帝曰：「臣一居嶺表，十載於茲，犬馬之情，不勝戀戀。

translations.literal: Zigai said to the emperor, "Your servant has dwelt south of the ranges for ten years now; the feeling of a dog or horse cannot overcome my longing.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai said to the emperor, "I have lived beyond the southern ranges for ten years now, and my devotion as your servant cannot overcome my longing for court.

sentences.zh: 願趨走闕庭，萬死無恨。」

translations.literal: I wish to hurry to the palace gates; I would have no regret even in death ten thousand times over."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to serve at the palace gates—even ten thousand deaths would leave me without regret."

sentences.zh: 帝賜物三百段，慰諭遣之，授銀青光祿大夫、武威太守，以善政聞。

translations.literal: The emperor granted him three hundred bolts of goods, comforted him, and sent him off, appointing him Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Administrator of Wuwei; he became known for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him three hundred bolts of goods, comforted him, and sent him on his way, appointing him Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and grand administrator of Wuwei, where his good governance became widely known.

sentences.zh: 大業三年入朝，帝引之內殿，特蒙褒美。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he came to court; the emperor led him into the inner hall and especially praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye he came to court; the emperor brought him into the inner hall and singled him out for special praise.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「設官之道，必在用賢，安人之術，莫如善政。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict saying, "The way to establish offices must lie in employing the worthy; the art of settling the people is nowhere better than in good government.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict saying, "The way to establish offices lies in employing the worthy, and the art of settling the people is nowhere better than good government.

sentences.zh: 龔、汲振德化于前，張、杜垂清風於後，共治天下，實資良守。

translations.literal: Gong and Ji spread moral transformation in earlier times; Zhang and Du handed down a pure breeze afterward; to govern the realm together truly depends on good prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Sheng and Ji Sui spread moral transformation in earlier times; Zhang Chang and Du Shi handed down a pure tradition afterward—to govern the realm together truly depends on capable prefects.

sentences.zh: 子蓋幹局通敏，操履清潔，自剖符西服，愛惠為先，撫道有方，寬猛得所。

translations.literal: Zigai is capable and penetrating in affairs, pure in conduct and bearing; since receiving his tally in the western service, he has put love and kindness first, governed the way with method, and balanced lenience and severity appropriately.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai is capable and quick-witted, pure in conduct and bearing; since taking up his commission in the west he has put kindness first, governed with sound method, and balanced lenience and severity fittingly.

sentences.zh: 處脂膏不潤其質，酌貪泉豈渝其性，故能治績克彰，課最之首。

translations.literal: Though placed amid fat and cream, it does not moisten his substance; though he dips from the Greedy Spring, how could it alter his nature? Therefore his administrative achievements stand forth clearly, and he ranks first in assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Though placed amid wealth and luxury, it does not stain his character; though he might dip from the Greedy Spring, how could it alter his nature? For this reason his administrative achievements stand out clearly, and he ranks first in assessment.

sentences.zh: 凡厥在位，莫匪王臣，若能人思奉職，各展其效，朕將冕旒垂拱，何憂不治哉！」

translations.literal: All who hold office are none other than the king's ministers; if each man thinks of fulfilling his duty and each displays his effect, I shall let my crown hang and fold my hands—what worry is there that the realm will not be well governed!"
translations.idiomatic: All who hold office are the king's ministers; if each man devotes himself to his duty and each displays his worth, I shall let my crown hang and fold my hands—what worry is there that the realm will not be well governed!"

sentences.zh: 於是進位金紫光祿大夫，賜物千段，太守如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, granted a thousand bolts of goods, and continued as Grand Administrator as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, granted a thousand bolts of goods, and continued as grand administrator as before.

sentences.zh: 五年，車駕西巡，將入吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the imperial carriage toured west, intending to enter Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor toured west, intending to enter Tuyuhun territory.

sentences.zh: 子蓋以彼多鄣氣，獻青木香以禦霧露。

translations.literal: Zigai, because that region had much miasmic vapor, presented eaglewood to ward off mist and dew.
translations.idiomatic: Because that region was thick with miasmic vapor, Zigai presented eaglewood to ward off mist and dew.

sentences.zh: 及帝還，謂之曰：「人道公清，定如此不？」

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he said to him, "People say you are pure—is it really so?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he said to him, "People say you are incorrupt—is it really so?"

sentences.zh: 子蓋謝曰：「臣安敢言清，止是小心不敢納賄耳。」

translations.literal: Zigai apologized and said, "Your servant would not dare claim to be pure; it is only that I am careful and dare not accept bribes."
translations.idiomatic: Zigai apologized and said, "I would not dare claim to be incorrupt; I am only careful and dare not accept bribes."

sentences.zh: 由此賜之口味百餘斛，又下詔曰：「導德齊禮，實惟共治，懲惡勸善，用明黜陟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted more than a hundred hu of delicacies, and another edict was issued saying, "Guiding virtue and harmonizing ritual are truly the means of joint governance; punishing evil and encouraging good are how promotion and demotion are made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was granted more than a hundred hu of delicacies, and another edict was issued saying, "Guiding virtue and harmonizing ritual are truly the means of joint governance; punishing evil and encouraging good are how promotion and demotion are made clear.

sentences.zh: 朕親巡河右，觀省人風，所曆郡縣，訪采治績，罕遵法度，多蹈刑網。

translations.literal: I personally toured the region west of the Yellow River to observe the customs of the people; in the commanderies and counties I passed through I inquired into administrative achievements—few observed the laws, and many fell into the penal net.
translations.idiomatic: I personally toured the region west of the Yellow River to observe the customs of the people; in the commanderies and counties I passed through I inquired into administrative achievements—few observed the laws, and many fell into the penal net.

sentences.zh: 而金紫光祿大夫、武威太守樊子蓋，執操清潔，處涅不渝，立身雅正，臨人以簡。

translations.literal: Yet Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Grand Administrator of Wuwei Fan Zigai holds his conduct pure and clean, stays unstained amid the black dye, stands upright in person, and treats people with simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Grand Administrator of Wuwei Fan Zigai holds his conduct pure and clean, stays unstained amid corruption, stands upright in person, and treats people with simplicity.

sentences.zh: 威惠兼舉，寬猛相資，故能畏而愛之，不嚴斯治。

translations.literal: He combines authority and kindness, balances lenience and severity, and therefore can make men fear yet love him—governing without harshness.
translations.idiomatic: He combines authority and kindness, balances lenience and severity, and therefore can make men fear yet love him—governing without harshness.

sentences.zh: 實字人之盛績，有國之良臣，宜加褒顯，以弘獎勵。

translations.literal: This is truly a great achievement for settling the people and a fine minister for the state; he should receive added praise and display to broaden encouragement and reward.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly a great achievement for settling the people and a fine minister for the state; he should receive added praise and display to broaden encouragement and reward.

sentences.zh: 可右光祿大夫，太守如故。」

translations.literal: He may be appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Right Seal, and continue as Grand Administrator as before."
translations.idiomatic: He may be appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Right Seal and continue as grand administrator as before."

sentences.zh: 賜縑千匹，粟麥二千斛。

translations.literal: He was granted a thousand bolts of silk and two thousand hu of grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a thousand bolts of silk and two thousand hu of grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 子蓋又自陳曰：「臣自南裔，即適西垂，常為外臣，未居內職。

translations.literal: Zigai also submitted a statement saying, "Your servant, from the southern marches, has gone straight to the western frontier; I have constantly been an outer official and have never held an inner post.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai also submitted a statement saying, "I came from the southern marches and went straight to the western frontier; I have constantly served as an outer official and have never held an inner post.

sentences.zh: 不得陪屬車，奉丹陛，溘死邊城，沒有遺恨。

translations.literal: I have been unable to follow the attendant carriage or attend the vermilion steps; to die suddenly on the border would leave me without regret.
translations.idiomatic: I have been unable to follow the attendant carriage or attend the vermilion steps; to die suddenly on the frontier would leave me without regret.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine this.
translations.idiomatic: Only may Your Majesty take note of this.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公侍朕則一人而已，委以西方則萬人之敵，宜識此心。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When you attend Us, you are Our one man alone; when We entrust the west to you, you are a match for ten thousand men—you should recognize this heart of Ours."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When you attend me, you are my one man alone; when I entrust the west to you, you are a match for ten thousand men—you should recognize what this means."

sentences.zh: 六年，帝避暑隴川宮，又雲欲幸河西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor took his summer retreat at Longchuan Palace and again spoke of wishing to visit Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the emperor took his summer retreat at Longchuan Palace and again spoke of wishing to visit Hexi.

sentences.zh: 子蓋傾望鑾輿，願巡郡境，帝知之，下詔曰：「卿夙懷恭順，深執誠心，聞朕西巡，欣然望幸。

translations.literal: Zigai looked eagerly for the imperial carriage and wished the emperor to tour his commandery; the emperor knew this and issued an edict saying, "You have long cherished respectful obedience and deeply held sincere devotion; hearing that We tour west, you gladly look for Our visit.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai looked eagerly for the imperial carriage and wished the emperor to tour his jurisdiction; the emperor knew this and issued an edict saying, "You have long cherished respectful obedience and deeply held sincere devotion; hearing that I tour west, you gladly look for my visit.

sentences.zh: 丹款之至，甚有可嘉。

translations.literal: Such sincerity of the red heart is very much to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Such sincerity of heart is very much to be praised.

sentences.zh: 宜保此純誠，克終其美。」

translations.literal: You should preserve this pure sincerity and bring your excellence to completion."
translations.idiomatic: You should preserve this pure sincerity and bring your excellence to completion."

sentences.zh: 是歲，朝于江都宮，帝謂之曰：「富貴不還故鄉，真衣繡夜行耳。」

translations.literal: That year he attended court at Jiangdu Palace; the emperor said to him, "Wealth and honor without returning to one's homeland is like wearing embroidered robes by night."
translations.idiomatic: That year he attended court at Jiangdu Palace; the emperor said to him, "Wealth and honor without returning to one's homeland is like wearing embroidered robes at night."

sentences.zh: 敕廬江郡設三千人會，賜米麥六千石，使謁墳墓，宴故老。

translations.literal: He ordered Lujiang Commandery to set out a gathering of three thousand men, granted six thousand shi of rice and wheat, and had him pay respects at his ancestral tombs and feast the elders of old.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Lujiang Commandery to set out a gathering of three thousand men, granted six thousand shi of rice and wheat, and had him pay respects at his ancestral tombs and feast the elders of his homeland.

sentences.zh: 當時榮之。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as glorious.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was regarded as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 還除民部尚書。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Minister of the People.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Minister of the People.

sentences.zh: 時處羅可汗及高昌王款塞，複以子蓋檢校武威太守，應接二蕃。

translations.literal: At the time Qaghan of the Western Turks and the King of Gaochang came to the border with tribute; Zigai was again made Acting Grand Administrator of Wuwei to receive the two foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the qaghan of the Western Turks and the king of Gaochang came to the border with tribute; Zigai was again made acting grand administrator of Wuwei to receive the two foreign states.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，征攝左武衛將軍，出長岑道。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was appointed on campaign as General of the Left Martial Guard and advanced by the Changcen route.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he was appointed on campaign as General of the Left Martial Guard and advanced by the Changcen route.

sentences.zh: 後以宿衛不行。

translations.literal: Later, because of palace guard duty, he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because of palace guard duty, he did not go.

sentences.zh: 進授左光祿大夫，尚書如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Left Seal, and continued as Minister as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Left Seal and continued as minister as before.

sentences.zh: 其年帝還東都，以子蓋為涿郡留守。

translations.literal: That year the emperor returned to the eastern capital and made Zigai Acting Commander of Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor returned to the eastern capital and made Zigai acting commander of Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 九年，車駕複幸遼東，命子蓋為東都留守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the imperial carriage again visited Liaodong and ordered Zigai to be Acting Commander of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the imperial carriage again visited Liaodong and ordered Zigai to be acting commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 屬楊玄感作逆，來逼王城，子蓋遣河南贊治裴弘策逆擊之，返為所敗，遂斬弘策以徇。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and came to press the royal city, Zigai sent Assistant Director of Henan Pei Hongce to strike him in reverse, but Hongce was defeated in turn; Zigai then executed Hongce to display to the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled and came to press the royal city, Zigai sent Assistant Director of Henan Pei Hongce to strike him, but Hongce was defeated in turn; Zigai then executed Hongce to display to the army.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒楊汪小有不恭，子蓋又將斬之。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Academy Yang Wang showed a slight lack of respect, and Zigai was again about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Academy Yang Wang showed a slight lack of respect, and Zigai was again about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 汪拜謝，頓首流血，久乃釋免。

translations.literal: Wang bowed in apology, knocking his head until it bled; only after a long time was he released and spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wang bowed in apology, knocking his head until it bled; only after a long time was he released and spared.

sentences.zh: 於是三軍莫不戰慄，將吏無敢仰視。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three armies all trembled in fear, and officers and clerks did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the three armies all trembled in fear, and officers and clerks did not dare look up.

sentences.zh: 玄感每盡銳攻城，子蓋徐設備禦，至輒摧破，故久不能克。

translations.literal: Xuangan each time deployed his best troops to attack the city; Zigai slowly made his preparations for defense, and whenever the enemy came he shattered them, so that for a long time they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan each time deployed his best troops to attack the city; Zigai slowly made his preparations for defense, and whenever the enemy came he shattered them, so that for a long time they could not take it.

sentences.zh: 會來護兒等救至，玄感解去。

translations.literal: When Lai Hu'er and others arrived with relief, Xuangan withdrew and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Hu'er and others arrived with relief, Xuangan withdrew and left.

sentences.zh: 子蓋凡所誅殺者數萬人。

translations.literal: In all, the persons Zigai executed numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the persons Zigai executed numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又檢校河南內史。

translations.literal: He was also made Acting Director of the Interior of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made acting director of the interior of Henan.

sentences.zh: 車駕至高陽，追詣行在所。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Gaoyang, he was summoned to pursue to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Gaoyang, he was summoned to pursue to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 既而引見，帝逆勞之曰：「昔高祖留蕭何于關西，光武委寇恂以河內，公其人也。」

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was granted audience; the emperor went forward to comfort him and said, "In former times Gaozu left Xiao He in Guanxi, and Guangwu entrusted Kou Xun with Henei—you are such a man.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was granted audience; the emperor went forward to comfort him and said, "In former times Emperor Gaozu left Xiao He in Guanxi, and Emperor Guangwu entrusted Kou Xun with Henei—you are such a man.

sentences.zh: 子蓋謝曰：「臣任重器小，寧可竊譬兩賢！

translations.literal: Zigai apologized and said, "Your servant's burden is heavy and his vessel small—how could I dare compare myself to those two worthies!
translations.idiomatic: Zigai apologized and said, "My burden is heavy and my vessel small—how could I dare compare myself to those two worthies!

sentences.zh: 但以陛下威靈，小盜不足除耳。」

translations.literal: It is only that, by Your Majesty's awesome might, a petty bandit is not enough to be eliminated."
translations.idiomatic: It is only that, by Your Majesty's awesome might, a petty bandit is not enough to be eliminated."

sentences.zh: 進位光祿大夫，封建安侯，尚書如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jian'an, and continued as Minister as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jian'an, and continued as minister as before.

sentences.zh: 賜縑三千匹，女樂五十人。

translations.literal: He was granted three thousand bolts of silk and fifty female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three thousand bolts of silk and fifty female musicians.

sentences.zh: 子蓋固讓，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Zigai firmly declined, but a gracious edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai firmly declined, but a gracious edict would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 帝顧謂子蓋曰：「朕遣越王留守東都，示以皇枝磐石；

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Zigai and said, "We dispatch the Prince of Yue to remain at the Eastern Capital as a sign that the imperial branch is a bedrock boulder;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Zigai and said, "I dispatch the Prince of Yue to remain at the Eastern Capital as a sign that the imperial branch is a bedrock boulder;

sentences.zh: 社稷大事，終以委公。

translations.literal: the great affairs of altars and grain We ultimately entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: the great affairs of state I ultimately entrust to you.

sentences.zh: 特宜持重，戈甲五百人而後出，此亦勇夫重閉之義也。

translations.literal: You should especially hold to weightiness; five hundred men in armor and arms should follow before you go out—this too is the meaning of the brave man who double-bars his door.
translations.idiomatic: You should especially hold to weightiness; five hundred men in armor and arms should follow before you go out—this too is the meaning of the brave man who double-bars his door.

sentences.zh: 無賴不軌者，便誅鋤之。

translations.literal: As for worthless and unprincipled men, execute and weed them out.
translations.idiomatic: As for worthless and unprincipled men, execute and weed them out.

sentences.zh: 凡可施行，無勞形跡。

translations.literal: Whatever may be carried out, do not trouble yourself over formalities.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever may be carried out, do not trouble yourself over formalities.

sentences.zh: 今為公別造玉麟符，以代銅獸。」

translations.literal: Now We have had made for you a separate jade lin tally to replace the bronze beast."
translations.idiomatic: Now I have had made for you a separate jade lin tally to replace the bronze beast."

sentences.zh: 又指越、代二王曰：「今以二孫委公與衛文升耳。

translations.literal: He also pointed to the two princes, Yue and Dai, and said, "Now We entrust these two grandsons to you and to Wei Wensheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also pointed to the two princes, Yue and Dai, and said, "Now I entrust these two grandsons to you and to Wei Wensheng.

sentences.zh: 宜選貞良宿德有方幅者教習之。

translations.literal: You should select upright and good men of established virtue and proper measure to instruct and teach them.
translations.idiomatic: You should select upright and good men of established virtue and proper measure to instruct and teach them.

sentences.zh: 動靜之節，宜思其可。」

translations.literal: In the norms of movement and stillness, you should consider what is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: In the norms of movement and stillness, you should consider what is fitting."

sentences.zh: 於是賜以良田、甲第。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted fine fields and a fine mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was granted fine fields and a fine mansion.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，車駕還東都，帝謂子蓋曰：「玄感之反，神明故以彰公赤心耳。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year the imperial carriage returned to the Eastern Capital; the emperor said to Zigai, "Xuangan's rebellion—the spirits therefore used it to display your red heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year the imperial carriage returned to the Eastern Capital; the emperor said to Zigai, "Xuangan's rebellion—the spirits therefore used it to display your loyal heart.

sentences.zh: 析珪進爵，宜有令謨。」

translations.literal: To break off a tally and advance in rank, there should be a fine pronouncement."
translations.idiomatic: To break off a tally and advance in rank, there should be a fine pronouncement."

sentences.zh: 是日下詔，進爵為濟公，言其功濟天下，特為立名，無此郡國也。

translations.literal: That day an edict was issued advancing his rank to Duke of Ji, meaning that his merit aided the realm; a title was specially established for him, and there was no such commandery or state.
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict was issued advancing his rank to Duke of Ji, meaning that his merit aided the realm; a title was specially established for him, and there was no such commandery or state.

sentences.zh: 賜縑三千匹，奴婢二十口。

translations.literal: He was granted three thousand bolts of silk and twenty male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted three thousand bolts of silk and twenty male and female servants.

sentences.zh: 後與蘇威、宇文述陪宴積翠亭，帝親以金杯屬子蓋酒，曰：「良算嘉謀，俟公後動，即以此杯賜公，用為永年之瑞。」

translations.literal: Later, together with Su Wei and Yuwen Shu, he attended a banquet at the Accumulated Emerald Pavilion; the emperor personally bestowed a golden cup upon Zigai with wine and said, "Fine plans and excellent counsel—we wait for your later move; with this cup We grant you, to serve as an omen of long years."
translations.idiomatic: Later, together with Su Wei and Yuwen Shu, he attended a banquet at the Accumulated Emerald Pavilion; the emperor personally bestowed a golden cup upon Zigai with wine and said, "Fine plans and excellent counsel—we wait for your later move; with this cup I grant you, to serve as an omen of long years."

sentences.zh: 並綺羅百匹。

translations.literal: He was also granted a hundred bolts of figured silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted a hundred bolts of figured silk.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從駕汾陽宮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed the imperial carriage to Fenyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he followed the imperial carriage to Fenyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 至於雁門，車駕為突厥所圍，頻戰不利。

translations.literal: When they reached Yanmen, the imperial carriage was surrounded by the Turks; battle after battle went badly.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Yanmen, the imperial carriage was surrounded by the Turks; battle after battle went badly.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以精騎潰圍而出，子蓋諫曰：「陛下萬乘之主，豈宜輕脫，一朝狼狽，雖悔不追。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to break out with picked cavalry; Zigai remonstrated, "Your Majesty is the lord of ten thousand chariots—how should you lightly cast yourself off? Once you fall into distress, even regret will not overtake it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to break out with picked cavalry; Zigai remonstrated, "Your Majesty is the lord of ten thousand chariots—how should you lightly cast yourself off? Once you fall into distress, even regret will not overtake it.

sentences.zh: 未若守城以挫其銳，四面徵兵，可立而待。

translations.literal: It is not as good as holding the city to blunt their edge; summon troops on all four sides, and they may be awaited standing.
translations.idiomatic: It is not as good as holding the city to blunt their edge; summon troops on all four sides, and they may be awaited standing.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦何所慮，乃欲身自突圍！」

translations.literal: What does Your Majesty have to worry about, that you wish to break through in person!"
translations.idiomatic: What does Your Majesty have to worry about, that you wish to break through in person!"

sentences.zh: 因垂泣，「願暫停遼東之役，以慰眾望。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept and said, "I wish to suspend the Liaodong campaign for the time being to comfort the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he wept and said, "I wish to suspend the Liaodong campaign for the time being to comfort the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: 聖躬親出慰撫，厚為勳格，人心自奮，不足為憂。」

translations.literal: If Your Sacred Person goes out in person to comfort and soothe them, and makes the reward scale generous, the people's hearts will rouse themselves of their own accord—there is nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Sacred Person goes out in person to comfort and soothe them, and makes the reward scale generous, the people's hearts will rouse themselves of their own accord—there is nothing to worry about."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 其後援兵稍至，虜乃引去。

translations.literal: Afterward relief troops gradually arrived, and the barbarians then withdrew and left.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward relief troops gradually arrived, and the barbarians then withdrew and left.

sentences.zh: 納言蘇威追論勳格太重，宜在斟酌。

translations.literal: Counselor Su Wei pursued the discussion that the reward scale was too heavy and should be weighed and adjusted.
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Su Wei pursued the discussion that the reward scale was too heavy and should be weighed and adjusted.

sentences.zh: 子蓋執奏不宜失信。

translations.literal: Zigai held to his memorial that one should not fail to keep faith.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai held to his memorial that one should not fail to keep faith.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公欲收物情邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Do you wish to win over popular sentiment?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do you wish to win over popular sentiment?

sentences.zh: 子蓋默然不敢對。

translations.literal: Zigai was silent and did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai was silent and did not dare reply.

sentences.zh: 從駕還東都。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage back to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the imperial carriage back to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時絳郡賊敬槃陀、柴保昌等阻兵數萬，汾、晉苦之。

translations.literal: At the time the bandits of Jiang Commandery Jing Pantuo, Chai Baochang, and others held weapons in the tens of thousands; Fen and Jin suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the bandits of Jiang Commandery Jing Pantuo, Chai Baochang, and others held weapons in the tens of thousands; Fen and Jin suffered from them.

sentences.zh: 詔令子蓋進討。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zigai to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zigai to advance and attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 于時人物殷阜，子蓋善惡無所分別，汾水之北，村塢盡焚之。

translations.literal: At the time the population was abundant; Zigai made no distinction between good and evil, and north of the Fen River he burned village stockades to the last.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the region was thick with people; Zigai made no distinction between the innocent and the guilty, and north of the Fen River he burned every village stockade.

sentences.zh: 百姓大駭，相率為盜。

translations.literal: The common people were greatly terrified and joined together as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The common people were terrified and rose up as bandits in droves.

sentences.zh: 其有歸首者，無少長悉坑之。

translations.literal: Those who came to surrender, without regard to young or old, he buried alive to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Those who came to surrender, young or old alike, he had buried alive without exception.

sentences.zh: 擁數萬之眾，經年不能破賊，有詔征還。

translations.literal: Though he held a host of tens of thousands, for years he could not break the bandits; an edict summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: Though he commanded tens of thousands, for years he could not defeat the rebels; an edict recalled him to court.

sentences.zh: 又將兵擊宜陽賊，以疾停，卒於京第，時年七十有二。

translations.literal: He was again to lead troops against the bandits of Yiyang, but halted on account of illness and died at his residence in the capital at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was again to lead troops against the bandits of Yiyang, but fell ill and halted; he died at his residence in the capital at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 上悲傷者久之，顧謂黃門侍郎裴矩曰：「子蓋臨終有何語？」

translations.literal: The emperor grieved for a long time and, turning to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Pei Ju, said, "What words did Zigai have at the end?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved for a long time and, turning to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Pei Ju, asked, "What did Zigai say before he died?"

sentences.zh: 矩對曰：「子蓋病篤，深恨雁門之恥。」

translations.literal: Ju replied, "Zigai was gravely ill and deeply regretted the disgrace at Yanmen."
translations.idiomatic: Ju replied, "Zigai was gravely ill and deeply regretted the disgrace at Yanmen."

sentences.zh: 帝聞而歎息，令百官就吊，賜縑三百匹，米五百斛，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰景。

translations.literal: On hearing this the emperor sighed and ordered all officials to go and offer condolences; he granted three hundred bolts of silk and five hundred hu of rice, posthumously appointed him Opening Office with ceremonial parity of the third rank, and gave the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this the emperor sighed and ordered all officials to offer condolences; he granted three hundred bolts of silk and five hundred hu of rice, posthumously appointed him opening-office third rank with ceremonial parity, and gave the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 會葬者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Those who attended the funeral numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand people attended his funeral.

sentences.zh: 武威民吏聞其死，莫不嗟痛，立碑頌德。

translations.literal: When the officials and people of Wuwei heard of his death, none failed to sigh in grief; they erected a stele to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials and people of Wuwei heard of his death, all mourned him; they erected a stele to praise his virtue.

sentences.zh: 子蓋無他權略，在軍持重，未嘗負敗，臨民明察，下莫敢欺。

translations.literal: Zigai had no other stratagems; in the army he was weighty and never suffered defeat; in governing the people he was sharp-sighted, and those below did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Zigai had no special stratagems; in the army he was steady and never suffered defeat; in governing the people he was sharp-sighted, and none beneath him dared deceive him.

sentences.zh: 然嚴酷少恩，果於殺戮，臨終之日，見斷頭鬼前後重遝為之厲雲。

translations.literal: Yet he was severe and cruel, sparing little kindness, and decisive in killing; on the day of his death he saw headless ghosts before and behind, piled in layers, haunting him—or so it was said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was severe and cruel, sparing little kindness, and decisive in killing; on the day of his death he was said to see headless ghosts before and behind, piled in layers, haunting him.

sentences.zh: ○史祥

translations.literal: ○ Shi Xiang
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiang

sentences.zh: 史祥，字世休，朔方人也。

translations.literal: Shi Xiang, style name Shixiu, was a native of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiang, whose style name was Shixiu, came from Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 父甯，周少司徒。

translations.literal: His father Ning was Junior Minister of Education under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning had served as Junior Minister of Education under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 祥少有文武才幹，仕周太子車右中士，襲爵武遂縣公。

translations.literal: Xiang in his youth had civil and military talent; he served Zhou as Right Attendant of the Heir Apparent's Carriage, and inherited the title Duke of Wusui.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang showed civil and military talent in his youth; he served as right attendant of the heir apparent's carriage under Zhou and inherited the title Duke of Wusui.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，拜儀同，領交州事，進爵陽城郡公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he was appointed Colonel with ceremonial parity, took charge of Jiaozhou affairs, and was advanced to Duke of Yangcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he was appointed a ceremonial colonel, took charge of Jiaozhou affairs, and was advanced to Duke of Yangcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祥在州頗有惠政。

translations.literal: Xiang in his province had considerable benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: In his province Xiang governed with considerable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 後數年，轉驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，從宜陽公王世積，以舟師出九江道，先鋒與陳人合戰，破之，進拔江州。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen he followed the Duke of Yiyang, Wang Shiji, leading a fleet out by the Jiujiang route; as vanguard he joined battle with the Chen forces, defeated them, and advanced to take Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Chen he followed the Duke of Yiyang, Wang Shiji, leading a fleet along the Jiujiang route; as vanguard he engaged the Chen forces, defeated them, and advanced to capture Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上聞而大悅，下詔曰：「朕以陳叔寶世為僭逆，挻虐生民，故命諸軍，救彼塗炭。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and was greatly pleased, and issued an edict saying, "We take Chen Shubao to have been a usurper for generations, cruel and oppressive toward the living people; therefore We ordered the armies to rescue them from fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard this and was greatly pleased, and issued an edict saying, "I take Chen Shubao to have been a usurper for generations, cruel and oppressive toward the people; therefore I ordered the armies to rescue them from misery.

sentences.zh: 小寇狼狽，顧恃江湖之險，遂敢泛舟楫擬抗王師。

translations.literal: The petty bandit, in distress, relied on the peril of rivers and lakes and dared to float boats and oars intending to resist the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: The petty rebel, hard pressed, relied on the peril of rivers and lakes and dared to float boats intending to resist the royal army.

sentences.zh: 公親率所部，應機奮擊，沉溺俘獲，厥功甚茂。

translations.literal: You personally led your command, struck according to opportunity with fierce attack, drowned and captured the enemy, and your achievement was very abundant.
translations.idiomatic: You personally led your command, struck at the right moment with fierce attack, drowned and captured the enemy, and your achievement was outstanding.

sentences.zh: 又聞帥旅進取江州。

translations.literal: We also hear that the army advances to take Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that the army is advancing to take Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行軍總管、襄邑公賀若弼既獲京口，新義公韓擒尋克姑熟。

translations.literal: Campaign General-in-Chief and Duke of Xiangyi He Ruobi has already taken Jingkou, and the Duke of Xinyi Han Qin soon took Guku.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign General-in-Chief and Duke of Xiangyi He Ruobi has already taken Jingkou, and the Duke of Xinyi Han Qin soon took Guku.

sentences.zh: 驃騎既渡江岸，所在橫行。

translations.literal: The General of Agile Cavalry has already crossed the river bank and everywhere marches at will.
translations.idiomatic: The general of agile cavalry has already crossed the south bank and marches at will wherever he goes.

sentences.zh: 晉王兵馬即入建業，清蕩吳、越，旦夕非遠。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin's soldiers and horses will soon enter Jianye; to clear Wu and Yue is not far, morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin's soldiers and horses will soon enter Jianye; to pacify Wu and Yue is only a matter of days.

sentences.zh: 驃騎高才壯志，是朕所知，善為經略，以取大賞，使富貴功名永垂竹帛也。」

translations.literal: The General of Agile Cavalry has lofty talent and great ambition—this We know; plan your strategy well to win a great reward, and make wealth, honor, and fame endure forever on bamboo and silk."
translations.idiomatic: The general of agile cavalry has lofty talent and great ambition—I know this well; plan your strategy wisely to win a great reward, and let wealth, honor, and fame endure forever in the histories.

sentences.zh: 進位上開府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Senior Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to senior opening-office general.

sentences.zh: 尋拜蘄州總管，未幾，征拜左領左右將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General-in-Chief of Qizhou; before long he was summoned and appointed General of the Left Guard of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed general-in-chief of Qizhou; before long he was summoned and appointed general of the left guard of the left.

sentences.zh: 後以行軍總管從晉王廣擊突厥于靈武，破之。

translations.literal: Later, as Campaign General-in-Chief, he followed the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, to strike the Turks at Lingwu and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as campaign general-in-chief, he followed the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, to strike the Turks at Lingwu and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，率兵屯弘化以備胡。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he led troops to garrison Honghua to guard against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou era he led troops to garrison Honghua to guard against the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時在東宮，遺祥書曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was in the Eastern Palace, he sent Xiang a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guang was crown prince in the Eastern Palace, he sent Xiang a letter saying:

sentences.zh: 將軍總戎塞表，胡虜清塵，秣馬休兵，猶事校獵，足使李廣慚勇，魏尚愧能，冠彼二賢，獨在吾子。

translations.literal: The general commands the army beyond the passes; the barbarians are cleared from the dust; though you rest the horses and lay down arms, you still go hunting—enough to make Li Guang ashamed of his courage and Wei Shang ashamed of his ability; you surpass those two worthies, and stand alone, my friend.
translations.idiomatic: General, you command the army beyond the passes; the barbarians are cleared from the frontier; though you rest your horses and lay down your arms, you still go hunting—enough to make Li Guang ashamed of his courage and Wei Shang ashamed of his ability; you surpass those two worthies and stand alone, my friend.

sentences.zh: 昔餘濫舉，推轂治兵，振皇靈於塞外，驅犬羊乎大漠。

translations.literal: In former days I was rashly promoted, pushed the chariot wheel and governed the army, shook the imperial majesty beyond the passes, and drove the dogs and sheep across the great desert.
translations.idiomatic: In former days I was rashly promoted, took charge of the army, shook imperial majesty beyond the passes, and drove the barbarians across the great desert.

sentences.zh: 于時同行軍旅，契闊戎旃，望龍城而衝冠，眄狼居而發憤。

translations.literal: At that time we marched together in the army, sharing hardships under the campaign banners, gazing at Longcheng and bristling with rage, looking toward Langjuxu and bursting with indignation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time we marched together in the army, sharing hardships under the campaign banners, gazing toward Longcheng and bristling with rage, looking toward Langjuxu and burning with indignation.

sentences.zh: 將軍英圖不世，猛氣無前，但物不遂心，<俛從事。

translations.literal: The general's heroic design is unmatched in the age, his fierce spirit without peer—but things do not accord with the heart, and he is forced to bow and submit to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: General, your heroic design is unmatched in the age and your fierce spirit without peer—but things do not accord with the heart, and you are forced to bow and submit to lesser affairs.

sentences.zh: 每一思此，我勞如何。

translations.literal: Each time I think of this, how great is my distress!
translations.idiomatic: Each time I think of this, how great is my distress!

sentences.zh: 將軍宿心素志，早同膠漆，久而敬之，方成魚水。

translations.literal: The general's long-held heart and plain ambition were early the same as glue and lacquer; with long respect they became like fish and water.
translations.idiomatic: General, your long-held heart and plain ambition were early as close as glue and lacquer; with long respect they became like fish and water.

sentences.zh: 近者陪隨鑾駕，言旋上京，本即述職南蕃，宣條下國，不悟皇鑒曲發，備位少陽，戰戰兢兢，如臨冰穀。

translations.literal: Recently, accompanying the imperial carriage, I spoke of returning to the upper capital; originally I was to report to duty in the southern marches and proclaim regulations in the lower states—but unawares the imperial regard bent down and I was installed in the place of Lesser Yang; trembling in fear, it is as if treading on ice over a valley.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, accompanying the imperial carriage, I spoke of returning to the capital; originally I was to report to duty in the southern marches and proclaim regulations in the lower states—but unawares the imperial regard bent down and I was installed as crown prince; trembling in fear, it is as if treading on ice over a valley.

sentences.zh: 至如建節邊境，征伐四方，褰帷作牧，綏撫百姓，上稟成規，下盡臣節，是所願也，是所甘心。

translations.literal: As for establishing insignia on the border, campaigning on the four sides, lifting the curtain as grand administrator, and soothing the common people—reporting above to the completed regulations and below fulfilling the minister's duty: these are what I wish, and what I give my heart to gladly.
translations.idiomatic: As for establishing insignia on the border, campaigning on the four sides, serving as grand administrator, and soothing the common people—reporting above to imperial regulations and below fulfilling a minister's duty: these are what I wish, and what I give my heart to gladly.

sentences.zh: 仰慕前修，庶得自效。

translations.literal: Looking up to former exemplars, I hope to bring forth my effect.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up to former exemplars, I hope to prove my worth.

sentences.zh: 謬其入守神器，元良萬國，身輕負重，何以克堪！

translations.literal: Erroneously I have entered to guard the divine vessel, the heir of ten thousand states; the body is light yet the burden heavy—how can I be equal to it!
translations.idiomatic: Erroneously I have entered to guard the throne, heir to ten thousand states; my person is slight yet the burden heavy—how can I bear it!

sentences.zh: 所望故人，匡其不逮。

translations.literal: What I look to from an old friend is to correct my shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: What I look to from an old friend is that you correct my shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 比監國多暇，養疾閑宮，厭北閣之端居，罷南皮之馳射。

translations.literal: Recently, while supervising the state I have had much leisure and nursed illness in the idle palace; I am weary of dwelling quietly in the northern pavilion and have ceased the galloping archery of Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, while supervising the state I have had much leisure and nursed illness in the idle palace; I am weary of dwelling quietly in the northern pavilion and have ceased the galloping archery of Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 博望之苑，既乏名賢，飛蓋之園，理乖終宴。

translations.literal: In the garden of Bowang there is a lack of famous worthies; in the park of Flying Canopy, feasting to the end is contrary to reason.
translations.idiomatic: In the garden of Bowang there is a lack of famous worthies; in the park of Flying Canopy, a feast to the end is contrary to reason.

sentences.zh: 親朋遠矣，琴書寂然，想望吾賢，疹如疾首。

translations.literal: Kin and friends are far; zither and books are silent; thinking of you, my worthy friend, it is like an illness in the head.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends are far away; zither and books are silent; thinking of you, my worthy friend, it is like an illness in the head.

sentences.zh: 祥答書曰：

translations.literal: Xiang replied in a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiang replied in a letter saying:

sentences.zh: 行人戾止，奉所賜況，恩紀綢繆，形于文墨。

translations.literal: The traveler has stopped; I receive what you bestowed, and your gracious regard, close and thick, is expressed in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Your messenger has arrived; I receive what you bestowed, and your gracious regard, close and intimate, is expressed in writing.

sentences.zh: 不悟飛雪增冰之地，忽載三陽，毳幙韋韝之鄉，俄聞九奏。

translations.literal: Unawares in a land where flying snow adds to ice, the three yangs suddenly load upon it; in a land of felt curtains and leather quivers, the nine performances are suddenly heard.
translations.idiomatic: Unawares in a land where flying snow adds to ice, the warmth of spring suddenly arrives; in a land of felt curtains and leather quivers, the music of court is suddenly heard.

sentences.zh: 精駭思越，莫知啟處。

translations.literal: My spirit is startled and my thoughts scattered; I do not know how to comport myself.
translations.idiomatic: My spirit is startled and my thoughts scattered; I do not know how to comport myself.

sentences.zh: 祥少不學軍旅，長遇升平，幸以先人緒餘，備職宿衛。

translations.literal: Xiang in his youth did not study military affairs; in his maturity he met an age of ascent and peace; fortunately, through my forebears' remaining estate, I fill a post in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: I in my youth did not study military affairs; in my maturity I met an age of peace; fortunately, through my forebears' remaining estate, I fill a post in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 懼駑蹇無致遠之用，朽薄非折衝之材，豈欲追蹤古人，語其優劣？

translations.literal: I fear that a lame nag has no use for going far, and rotten thinness is not material for breaking the foe—how would I wish to follow the tracks of the ancients and speak of superiority or inferiority?
translations.idiomatic: I fear that a lame nag has no use for going far, and a rotten plank is not material for breaking the foe—how would I wish to follow the ancients and speak of superiority or inferiority?

sentences.zh: 曩者王師薄伐，天人受脤，絕漠揚旌，威震海外。

translations.literal: In former days the royal army made a shallow campaign; Heaven and man received the sacrificial meat; banners were raised across the desert, and awe shook the lands beyond the seas.
translations.idiomatic: In former days the royal army campaigned; Heaven and man received the sacrificial meat; banners were raised across the desert, and awe shook the lands beyond the seas.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，猛將如雲，謀夫如雨。

translations.literal: At that time fierce generals were like clouds, and strategists like rain.
translations.idiomatic: At that time fierce generals were like clouds, and strategists like rain.

sentences.zh: 至若祥者，列于卒伍，預聞指蹤之規，得免逗遛之責，循涯揣分，實為幸甚。

translations.literal: As for Xiang, he was ranked among the ranks of soldiers, heard beforehand the rules of direction and control, and was spared the blame of delay—measuring the bank and estimating his portion, it was truly very fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: As for me, I was ranked among the soldiers, heard beforehand the rules of command, and was spared the blame of delay—measuring my portion against my capacity, it was truly very fortunate.

sentences.zh: 爰以情喻雷、陳，事方劉、葛，信聖人之屈己，非庸人之擬議。

translations.literal: Therefore with feeling I compare you to Lei and Chen, and the matter to Liu and Ge; I believe a sage bends himself—this is not a matter for mediocre men to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore with feeling I compare you to Lei and Chen, and the matter to Liu and Ge; I believe a sage bends himself—this is not a matter for mediocre men to discuss.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 川澤之大，汙潦攸歸，松柏之高，蔦蘿斯托。

translations.literal: The great rivers and marshes—muddy runoff all return to them; the height of pine and cypress—dodder and creepers all cling to them.
translations.idiomatic: Great rivers and marshes—all muddy runoff returns to them; tall pine and cypress—all creepers cling to them.

sentences.zh: 微心眷眷，孟侯所知也。

translations.literal: My slight heart's deep regard—the Lord of Meng knows it.
translations.idiomatic: My slight heart's deep regard—my lord knows it.

sentences.zh: 抑惟體元良之德，煥重離之暉，三善克修，萬邦以正。

translations.literal: Moreover, embodying the virtue of the worthy heir, brightening the radiance of double departure, the three excellences are fully cultivated, and the ten thousand states are set right.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, embodying the virtue of the worthy heir, brightening the radiance of the crown, the three excellences are fully cultivated, and the ten thousand states are set right.

sentences.zh: 斯固道高周誦，契葉商皓，豈在管蠡所能窺測！

translations.literal: This is truly a Way higher than the Zhou recitation, a bond like the leaves of Shang and Hao—how could a measuring tube or gourd dipper glimpse it!
translations.idiomatic: This is truly a Way higher than the Zhou recitation, a bond like the leaves of Shang and Hao—how could a measuring tube glimpse it!

sentences.zh: 伏承監國多暇，養德怡神，咀嚼六經，逍遙百氏。

translations.literal: I respectfully hear that while supervising the state you have much leisure, nurturing virtue and pleasing the spirit, chewing the Six Classics and roaming among the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully hear that while supervising the state you have much leisure, nurturing virtue and pleasing the spirit, studying the Six Classics and roaming among the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 追西園之愛客，眷南皮之出遊，疇昔之恩，無忘造次。

translations.literal: Following the beloved guests of the Western Garden, cherishing the outings of Nanpi—the kindness of former days, do not forget it even in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Following the beloved guests of the Western Garden, cherishing the outings of Nanpi—the kindness of former days, do not forget it even in haste.

sentences.zh: 祥自忝式遏，載罹寒暑，身在邊隅，情馳魏闕。

translations.literal: Xiang since taking on the task of repelling invaders has passed through cold and heat; his body is on the border corner, but his feelings race to the Wei capital.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking on the task of repelling invaders I have passed through cold and heat; my body is on the border, but my feelings race to the capital.

sentences.zh: 每至清風夕起，朗月孤照，想鳴葭之啟路，思托乘于後車。

translations.literal: Whenever the clear wind rises in the evening and the bright moon shines alone, I think of the reed pipes opening the road and wish to ride in the rear carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the clear wind rises in the evening and the bright moon shines alone, I think of the reed pipes opening the road and wish to ride in the rear carriage.

sentences.zh: 塞表京華，山川悠遠，瞻望浮雲，伏增潸結。

translations.literal: Beyond the passes the capital is far; mountains and rivers are distant; gazing at floating clouds, I bow and increase my tears.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the passes the capital is far; mountains and rivers stretch between us; gazing at floating clouds, I bow and my tears increase.

sentences.zh: 太子甚親遇之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent treated him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince treated him with great intimacy.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，漢王諒發兵作亂，遣其將綦良自滏口徇黎陽，塞白馬津，餘公理自太行下河內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, the Prince of Han, Liang, raised troops in rebellion and sent his generals Qi Liang from Fukou to strike toward Liyang and block the Baima Ford, while Yu Gongli came down from the Taihang Mountains into Henei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang acceded, the Prince of Han, Yang Liang, raised troops in rebellion and sent his generals Qi Liang from Fukou to strike toward Liyang and block the Baima Ford, while Yu Gongli came down from the Taihang Mountains into Henei.

sentences.zh: 帝以祥為行軍總管，軍于河陰，久不得濟。

translations.literal: The emperor made Xiang Campaign General-in-Chief; he encamped at Heyin and for a long time could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Xiang campaign general-in-chief; he encamped at Heyin and for a long time could not cross the river.

sentences.zh: 祥謂軍吏曰：「餘公理輕而無謀，才用素不足稱，又新得志，謂其眾可恃。

translations.literal: Xiang said to the army officers, "Yu Gongli is light and without strategy; his talent and ability from the outset are not enough to be praised; moreover he has newly gained his aim and thinks his host can be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said to the army officers, "Yu Gongli is rash and without strategy; his talent and ability have never been noteworthy; moreover he has newly gained his aim and thinks his host can be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 恃眾必驕。

translations.literal: To rely on a host is surely to become arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: To rely on numbers is surely to become arrogant.

sentences.zh: 且河北人先不習兵，所謂擁市人而戰。

translations.literal: Moreover the people of Hebei from the first did not practice arms—it is what is called leading market people into battle.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the people of Hebei have never practiced arms—it is what is called leading market people into battle.

sentences.zh: 以吾籌之，不足圖也。」

translations.literal: By my reckoning, he is not enough to be plotted against."
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning, he is not worth plotting against.

sentences.zh: 乃令軍中修攻具，公理使諜知之，果屯兵于河陽內城以備祥。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the army to prepare siege engines; Gongli sent spies to learn of it and indeed massed troops in the inner city of Heyang to guard against Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered the army to prepare siege engines; Gongli sent spies to learn of it and indeed massed troops in the inner city of Heyang to guard against Xiang.

sentences.zh: 祥於是艤船南岸，公理聚甲以當之。

translations.literal: Xiang thereupon moored his boats on the south bank; Gongli gathered armor to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang thereupon moored his boats on the south bank; Gongli gathered armor to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 祥乃簡精銳於下流潛渡，公理率眾拒之。

translations.literal: Xiang then selected picked troops to cross secretly downstream; Gongli led his host to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang then selected picked troops to cross secretly downstream; Gongli led his host to resist him.

sentences.zh: 祥至須水，兩軍相對，公理未成列，祥縱擊，大破之。

translations.literal: When Xiang reached the Xu River the two armies faced each other; Gongli had not yet formed his ranks when Xiang loosed an attack and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang reached the Xu River the two armies faced each other; Gongli had not yet formed his ranks when Xiang attacked and greatly defeated him.

sentences.zh: 東趣黎陽討綦良等。

translations.literal: He pressed east toward Liyang to attack Qi Liang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed east toward Liyang to attack Qi Liang and the others.

sentences.zh: 良列陣以待，兵未接，良棄軍而走。

translations.literal: Liang drew up his ranks to await him; before the troops had joined battle, Liang abandoned his army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liang drew up his ranks to await him; before the troops had joined battle, Liang abandoned his army and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是其眾大潰，祥縱兵乘之，殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon his host collapsed in great disorder; Xiang loosed his troops to pursue them and killed more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his host collapsed in great disorder; Xiang loosed his troops to pursue them and killed more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 進位上大將軍，賜縑彩七千段，女妓十人，良馬二十匹。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Senior General-in-Chief, granted seven thousand bolts of figured silk, ten female musicians, and twenty fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to senior general-in-chief, granted seven thousand bolts of figured silk, ten female musicians, and twenty fine horses.

sentences.zh: 轉太僕卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜祥詩曰：「伯煚朝寄重，夏侯親遇深。

translations.literal: The emperor once bestowed a poem on Xiang saying, "Bo Jiu's court commission is weighty; Xiahou's intimate regard is deep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once bestowed a poem on Xiang saying, "Bo Jiu's court commission is weighty; Xiahou's intimate regard is deep.

sentences.zh: 貴耳唯聞古，賤目詎知今，早厓勁草質，久有背淮心。

translations.literal: The noble ear hears only the ancients; the base eye—how would it know the present? Early the cliff grass's tough quality; long has there been a heart to turn its back on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The noble ear hears only the ancients; the base eye—how would it know the present? Early the tough quality of cliff grass; long has there been a heart to turn away from the Huai.

sentences.zh: 掃逆黎山外，振旅河之陰。

translations.literal: Sweeping the rebels beyond Lishan, shaking the army north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Sweeping the rebels beyond Lishan, shaking the army north of the river.

sentences.zh: 功已書王府，留情《太僕箴》。」

translations.literal: Merit is already recorded in the royal house; affection remains for the "Minister of the Stud's Admonition."
translations.idiomatic: Merit is already recorded in the royal house; affection remains for the "Minister of the Stud's Admonition."

sentences.zh: 祥上表辭謝，帝降手詔曰：「昔歲勞公問罪河朔，賊爾日塞兩關之路，據倉阻河，百姓脅從，人亦眾矣。

translations.literal: Xiang submitted a memorial declining thanks; the emperor sent a handwritten edict saying, "In former years We labored you to question guilt in Heshuo; the bandit at that time blocked the road through the two passes, held the granary and blocked the river—the common people were compelled to follow, and the men were also numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang submitted a memorial declining thanks; the emperor sent a handwritten edict saying, "In former years I labored you to punish guilt in Heshuo; the rebel at that time blocked the road through the two passes, held the granary and blocked the river—the common people were compelled to follow, and his forces were also numerous.

sentences.zh: 公竭誠奮勇，一舉克定。

translations.literal: You exhausted your sincerity and exerted your courage; in one move you conquered and settled it.
translations.idiomatic: You exhausted your sincerity and exerted your courage; in one move you conquered and settled it.

sentences.zh: 《詩》不雲乎：'喪亂既平，既安且寧。

translations.literal: Does not the Odes say, "The turmoil and disorder are already pacified; already there is peace and rest."
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Odes say, "The turmoil and disorder are already pacified; already there is peace and rest."

sentences.zh: '非英才大略，其孰能與於此邪！

translations.literal: Unless a heroic talent of great design, who could share in this!
translations.idiomatic: Unless a heroic talent of great design, who could share in this!

sentences.zh: 故聊示所懷，亦何謝也。」

translations.literal: Therefore We briefly show Our feelings—what is there to thank for?"
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I briefly show my feelings—what is there to thank for?"

sentences.zh: 尋遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Director of Guests.

sentences.zh: 時突厥啟民可汗請朝，帝遣祥迎接之。

translations.literal: At the time Qaghan Qimin of the Turks requested an audience; the emperor sent Xiang to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qaghan Qimin of the Turks requested an audience; the emperor sent Xiang to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，祥率眾出間道擊虜，破之，俘男女千餘口。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Tuyuhun, Xiang led his host out by a bypath to strike the barbarians, defeated them, and captured more than a thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Tuyuhun, Xiang led his host out by a bypath to strike the barbarians, defeated them, and captured more than a thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢六十人，馬三百匹。

translations.literal: He was granted sixty male and female servants and three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted sixty male and female servants and three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 進位左光祿大夫，拜左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Left Seal and appointed General of the Left Martial Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Left Seal and appointed General of the Left Martial Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及遼東之役，出蹋頓道，不利而還。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he advanced by the Tadun route, met with ill fortune, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he advanced by the Tadun route, met with ill fortune, and returned.

sentences.zh: 由是除名為民。

translations.literal: For this reason he was struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was removed from office and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 俄拜燕郡太守，被賊高開道所圍，祥稱疾不視事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yan Commandery, was besieged by the bandit Gao Kaidao, and Xiang claimed illness and did not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made governor of Yan Commandery, but when the rebel Gao Kaidao besieged him, Xiang feigned illness and refused to take up his duties.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，開道甚禮之。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Kaidao treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, Kaidao treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 會開道與羅藝通和，送祥於涿郡，卒於途。

translations.literal: When Kaidao made peace with Luo Yi, he sent Xiang to Zhuo Commandery, and Xiang died on the way.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaidao reached an accord with Luo Yi, he sent Xiang toward Zhuo Commandery, but Xiang died en route.

sentences.zh: 有子義隆，永年令。

translations.literal: He had a son Yilong, who was magistrate of Yongnian.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son, Yilong, who served as magistrate of Yongnian.

sentences.zh: 祥兄雲，字世高，弟威，字世儀，並有幹局。

translations.literal: Xiang's elder brother Yun, style name Shigao, and younger brother Wei, style name Shiyi, both had administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's elder brother Yun, styled Shigao, and his younger brother Wei, styled Shiyi, both possessed real administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 雲官至萊州刺史、武平縣公，威官至武賁郎將、武當縣公。

translations.literal: Yun rose to Inspector of Laizhou and Marquis of Wuping County; Wei rose to General of the Martial Tiger Guard and Marquis of Wudang County.
translations.idiomatic: Yun reached the posts of inspector of Laizhou and Marquis of Wuping, while Wei rose to general of the Martial Tiger Guard and Marquis of Wudang.

sentences.zh: ○元壽

translations.literal: ○ Yuan Shou
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shou

sentences.zh: 元壽，字長壽，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shou, style name Changshou, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shou, whose style name was Changshou, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖敦，魏侍中、邵陵王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dun was chamberlain-attendant-in-ordinary under Wei and Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dun had served the Wei as chamberlain-attendant-in-ordinary and as Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 父寶，周涼州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Bao was Governor of Liang Province under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao had been governor of Liang Province under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 壽少孤，性仁孝，九歲喪父，哀毀骨立，宗族鄉黨鹹異之。

translations.literal: Shou lost his father early; his nature was benevolent and filial. At nine he lost his father, and his grief wasted him to skin and bone; clan and village all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was orphaned young and by nature gentle and filial. When he lost his father at nine, grief left him wasted to skin and bone, and kin and neighbors alike were astonished.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His filial devotion to his mother became widely known.

sentences.zh: 及長，方直，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was upright and square, and broadly read the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he proved upright and principled, with a solid grounding in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 周武成初，封隆城縣侯，邑千戶，保定四年，改封儀隴縣侯，授儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng under Zhou he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longcheng with a fief of one thousand households; in the fourth year of Baoding he was changed to Marquis of Yilong and granted Third Rank Commissioner with Ceremonial Parity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Wucheng's reign he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longcheng with a fief of one thousand households; in Baoding year 4 he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yilong and made a third-rank commissioner with ceremonial parity.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，議伐陳，以壽有思理，奉使於淮浦監修船艦，以強濟見稱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, when the conquest of Chen was under discussion, because Shou had thoughtful reasoning he was sent on mission to the Huai coast to supervise the building of ships, and was praised for robust assistance.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaihuang era, when plans were made to attack Chen, Shou's sound judgment earned him a mission to the Huai shore to oversee shipbuilding, where his energetic effectiveness won praise.

sentences.zh: 四年，參督漕渠之役，授尚書主爵侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he took part in supervising the canal project and was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel for Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he helped supervise work on the canal and was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Personnel for enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 八年，從晉王伐陳，除行台左丞，兼領元帥府屬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed the Prince of Jin in the attack on Chen, was appointed Left Assistant of the Mobile Secretariat, and concurrently held a post in the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he followed the Prince of Jin against Chen, becoming left assistant of the mobile secretariat while also serving on the marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 及平陳，拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was appointed Left Assistant of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was pacified, he was appointed left assistant of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗出苑觀射，文武並從焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once went out to the park to watch archery, and civil and military officials all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once went out to the archery park, with civil and military officials in attendance.

sentences.zh: 開府蕭摩訶妻患且死，奏請遣子向江南收其家產，御史見而不言。

translations.literal: The wife of Acting Grand General Xiao Mohe was ill and near death; he memorialized requesting to send his son to Jiangnan to recover family property, and the censor saw this but said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Acting grand general Xiao Mohe's wife lay gravely ill; he petitioned to send his son to Jiangnan to recover family property, yet the censor who witnessed it kept silent.

sentences.zh: 壽奏劾之曰：

translations.literal: Shou memorialized to impeach him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shou submitted an impeachment memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天道不言，功成四序，聖皇垂拱，任在百司。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the Way of Heaven is wordless, yet its achievement completes the four seasons; the sage emperor reigns at ease, and the burden rests on the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Heaven's Way needs no words, yet through it the four seasons run their course; the sage emperor governs without strain, and responsibility falls on the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 御史之官，義存糾察，直繩莫舉，憲典誰寄？

translations.literal: The office of censor exists to investigate and correct; if the straight line is not applied, upon whom can the penal code be entrusted?
translations.idiomatic: The censor's charge is investigation and correction; if the straight cord of law is never raised, to whom can the penal code be entrusted?

sentences.zh: 今月五日，鑾輿徙蹕，親臨射苑，開府儀同三司蕭摩訶幸廁朝行，預觀盛禮，奏稱請遣子世略暫往江南重收家產。

translations.literal: On the fifth of this month the imperial carriage moved and halted; the emperor personally attended the archery park. Acting Grand General with Third Rank Ceremonial Parity Xiao Mohe took his place in the imperial procession, participated in viewing the grand ceremony, and memorialized requesting to send his son Shilüe temporarily to Jiangnan to again recover family property.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth of this month the imperial procession moved to the archery park, where the emperor presided in person. Xiao Mohe, acting grand general with third-rank ceremonial parity, marched in the imperial train, watched the grand rite, and petitioned to send his son Shilüe temporarily to Jiangnan to recover family property once more.

sentences.zh: 妻安遇患，彌留有日，安若長逝，世略不合此行。

translations.literal: His wife An has fallen ill; her lingering illness has lasted days. If An should pass away, Shilüe ought not undertake this journey.
translations.idiomatic: His wife An is dangerously ill and has lingered for days; should she die, Shilüe should not be sent away on such a journey.

sentences.zh: 竊以人倫之義，伉儷為重，資愛之道，烏鳥弗虧。

translations.literal: I privately consider that in human relations husband and wife are weightiest, and in the way of nurturing love not even the crow falls short.
translations.idiomatic: In the bonds of human life, nothing weighs more than husband and wife; in the duty of cherishing those we love, not even the filial crow falls short.

sentences.zh: 摩訶遠念資財，近忘匹好，又命其子舍危惙之母，為聚斂之行。

translations.literal: Mohe thinks of distant wealth, forgets his near conjugal bond, and moreover orders his son to abandon his dangerously ill mother for a mission of gathering wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe broods over distant wealth while forgetting the wife at his side, and would send his son away from a dying mother on a mission of greed.

sentences.zh: 一言才發，名教頓盡。

translations.literal: As soon as one word was spoken, moral teaching was instantly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: With a single utterance he had undone the whole fabric of moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 而兼殿內侍御史臣韓微之等，親所聞見，竟不彈糾。

translations.literal: Yet the concurrent Palace Attendant Censor Han Weizhi and others personally heard and saw this, yet ultimately did not impeach.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Han Weizhi, concurrent palace attendant censor, and others who heard and saw it with their own ears and eyes never impeached him.

sentences.zh: 若知非不舉，事涉阿縱；

translations.literal: If they knew it was wrong and did not act, the matter involves indulgence and laxity;
translations.idiomatic: If they knew it was wrong and kept silent, that is connivance and dereliction;

sentences.zh: 如不以為非，豈關理識？

translations.literal: if they did not consider it wrong, where does reason and discernment come in?
translations.idiomatic: if they did not think it wrong, what then becomes of judgment and moral sense?

sentences.zh: 謹按儀同三司、太子左庶子、檢校治書侍御史臣劉行本，出入宮省，備蒙任遇，攝職憲台，時月稍久，庶能整肅纓冕，澄清風教。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that Third Rank Commissioner with Ceremonial Parity, Left Assistant to the Crown Prince, and Acting Director of the Bureau of Documents and Attendant Censor Liu Xingben, going in and out of the palace offices, has fully received trust and favor; holding an acting post at the Censorate for some months, he ought to be able to put in order the ranks and caps and clarify customs and moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that Liu Xingben, third-rank commissioner with ceremonial parity, left assistant to the crown prince, and acting director of the Bureau of Documents and attendant censor, moving in and out of the palace offices, has enjoyed full trust; after months in charge of the censorate, he ought to have restored official decorum and clarified public morals.

sentences.zh: 而在法司，虧失憲體，瓶罄罍恥，何所逃愆！

translations.literal: Yet in the legal office he has lost the body of the penal code; when the jug is empty and the jar is disgraced, from what can guilt escape!
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the legal office he has failed the penal code itself; when the lesser vessel is empty, the greater is shamed—how can he escape blame?

sentences.zh: 臣謬膺朝寄，忝居左轄，無容寢默，謹以狀聞。

translations.literal: Your subject wrongly receives the court's trust and humbly holds the left vice-directorship; I cannot remain silent and respectfully submit this report.
