translations.idiomatic: I have wrongly received the court's trust and hold the left vice-directorship; I cannot keep silent, and respectfully submit this report.

sentences.zh: 其行本、微之等，請付大理。

translations.literal: Liu Xingben, Weizhi, and the others I request be handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Xingben, Weizhi, and the others be referred to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial and accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 尋授太常少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 數年，拜基州刺史，在任有公廉之稱。

translations.literal: Several years later he was appointed Governor of Jizhou; in office he had a reputation for fairness and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he became governor of Jizhou, where his fair and incorrupt conduct won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 入為太府少卿。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 進位開府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting grand general.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，漢王諒舉兵反，左僕射楊素為行軍元帥，壽為長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, the Prince of Han Liang raised troops in rebellion; Left Vice Director Yang Su was campaign marshal, and Shou was chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, Prince Liang of Han rebelled; left vice director Yang Su served as campaign marshal, with Shou as his chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 壽每遇賊，為士卒先，以功授大將軍，遷太府卿。

translations.literal: Whenever Shou encountered the enemy he took the lead among the soldiers; for his merit he was granted the rank of General-in-Chief and transferred to Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shou met the enemy he led from the front; for his service he was made general-in-chief and transferred to director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜內史令，從帝西討吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and followed the emperor west on campaign against Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was appointed director of the Palace Secretariat and accompanied the emperor west against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 壽率眾屯金山，東西連營三百餘裡，以圍渾主。

translations.literal: Shou led troops to encamp at Jinshan, connecting camps east and west for more than three hundred li to besiege the Tuyuhun ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Shou encamped at Jinshan with camps stretching more than three hundred li east and west to surround the Tuyuhun ruler.

sentences.zh: 及還，拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Upon his return he was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made right grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 七年，兼左翊衛將軍，從征遼東，行至涿郡，遇疾卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he concurrently served as General of the Left Wing Guard, followed the campaign to Liaodong, reached Zhuo Commandery, fell ill, and died at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, also serving as general of the Left Wing Guard, he joined the Liaodong campaign; he reached Zhuo Commandery, fell ill, and died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 帝悼惜焉，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned and regretted it, and wept for him exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply and wept over him at length.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書右僕射、光祿大夫，諡曰景。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; his posthumous name was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the posts of right vice director of the Ministry of Works and grand master of splendid happiness, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子敏，頗有才辯，而輕險多詐。

translations.literal: His son Min was quite talented and eloquent, but frivolous, rash, and much given to deceit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min was clever and articulate, but reckless, treacherous, and much given to deceit.

sentences.zh: 壽卒後，帝追思之，擢敏為守內史舍人，而交通博徒，數漏泄省中語。

translations.literal: After Shou died, the emperor, remembering him, promoted Min to Acting Palace Secretariat Attendant, but Min associated with gamblers and repeatedly leaked words from within the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Shou's death the emperor, thinking of his father, raised Min to acting palace secretariat attendant, but Min consorted with gamblers and repeatedly leaked confidential court business.

sentences.zh: 化及之反也，敏創其謀，偽授內史侍郎，為沈光所殺。

translations.literal: When Huaji rebelled, Min originated the plot, was falsely appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, and was killed by Shen Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Wen Huaji rebelled, Min helped hatch the plot, was given the false title of vice director of the Palace Secretariat, and was killed by Shen Guang.

sentences.zh: ○楊義臣

translations.literal: ○ Yang Yichen
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yichen

sentences.zh: 楊義臣，代人也，本姓尉遲氏。

translations.literal: Yang Yichen was a man of Dai and originally bore the surname Yuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yichen came from Dai and was originally of the Yuchi clan.

sentences.zh: 父崇，仕周為儀同大將軍，以兵鎮恆山。

translations.literal: His father Chong served Zhou as Third Rank Commissioner Grand General and garrisoned troops at Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong served Northern Zhou as a third-rank commissioner grand general and held troops at Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 時高祖為定州總管，崇知高祖相貌非常，每自結納，高祖甚親待之。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu was Governor-General of Dingzhou; Chong knew Gaozu's appearance was extraordinary and each time personally cultivated ties with him, and Gaozu treated him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was governor-general of Dingzhou, Chong saw that his bearing was extraordinary and deliberately cultivated his favor; the future emperor treated him with great warmth.

sentences.zh: 及為丞相，尉迥作亂，崇以宗族之故，自囚於獄，遣使請罪。

translations.literal: When he became Chancellor, Yu Wei rebelled; Chong, because of clan ties, imprisoned himself and sent a messenger to plead guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen became chancellor, Yuchi Wei rebelled; because they were kin, Chong had himself imprisoned and sent a messenger to confess his family's guilt.

sentences.zh: 高祖下書慰諭之，即令馳驛入朝，恆置左右。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued a writ to comfort and instruct him and immediately ordered him to come post-haste to court, always keeping him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a letter of reassurance, then summoned him post-haste to court and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，封秦興縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinxing County.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Kaihuang he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinxing County.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，從行軍總管達奚長儒擊突厥于周盤，力戰而死。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he followed Campaign Governor-General Daxi Changru in striking the Turks at Zhoupan, fought fiercely, and died.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he followed campaign governor-general Daxi Changru against the Turks at Zhoupan, fought fiercely, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、豫州刺史，以義臣襲崇官爵。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted General-in-Chief and Governor of Yuzhou, and Yichen inherited Chong's offices and title.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general-in-chief and governor of Yuzhou, and Yichen inherited his offices and title.

sentences.zh: 時義臣尚幼，養于宮中，年未弱冠，奉詔宿衛如千牛者數年，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: At the time Yichen was still young and was raised in the palace; before reaching capped age he attended imperial guard by edict like the Thousand-Ox guards for several years, and rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen was still a boy and was reared in the palace; before he came of age he served by imperial order in the palace guard like the Thousand-Ox guards for several years, with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 上嘗從容言及恩舊，顧義臣嗟歎久之，因下詔曰：「朕受命之初，群凶未定，明識之士，有足可懷。

translations.literal: The emperor once spoke at ease of old favors, turned to Yichen and sighed long, then issued an edict saying: "At the beginning when I received the Mandate, many villains were not yet settled, and men of clear insight had much to recommend them.
translations.idiomatic: Once, speaking fondly of old companions, the emperor turned to Yichen and sighed at length, then issued an edict: "When I first received the Mandate, the realm was still unsettled, and clear-sighted men were men one could truly rely upon.

sentences.zh: 尉義臣與尉迥，本同骨肉，既狂悖作亂鄴城，其父崇時在常山，典司兵甲，與迥鄰接，又是至親，知逆順之理，識天人之意，即陳丹款，慮染惡徒，自執有司，請歸相府。

translations.literal: Yuchi Yichen and Yuchi Wei were originally of the same flesh and bone; when Wei recklessly rebelled at Ye, his father Chong was then at Changshan in charge of arms, adjacent to Wei and also closest kin. Knowing the principle of obedience versus rebellion and understanding Heaven and men's intent, he immediately declared loyal sincerity, fearing contamination by evil followers, imprisoned himself before the authorities, and requested to return to the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Yichen and Yuchi Wei were blood kin; when Wei rose in mad rebellion at Ye, his father Chong was at Changshan commanding troops on Wei's border and was his closest relative. Knowing the difference between loyalty and treason and reading Heaven's intent, he at once declared his faith, feared being tainted by rebels, surrendered himself to the law, and asked to answer at the chancellor's court.

sentences.zh: 及北夷內侵，橫戈制敵，輕生重義，馬革言旋。

translations.literal: When the northern barbarians invaded within, he brandished his spear to control the enemy, lightly valued life and heavily valued righteousness, and returned wrapped in horse hide.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern barbarians invaded, he took up arms against the foe, held righteousness dearer than life, and fell on campaign to return only in a horse-hide shroud.

sentences.zh: 操表存亡，事貫幽顯，雖高官大賞，延及於世，未足表松筠之志，彰節義之門。

translations.literal: Conduct extending through life and death, matters penetrating hidden and manifest—though high offices and great rewards extending to later generations are not sufficient to express pine-and-cypress resolve or illuminate the gate of integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct bridged life and death and reached through this world and the next; though high rank and rich reward passed down through his house, they were not enough to honor his steadfast resolve or burnish the name of his loyal family.

sentences.zh: 義臣可賜姓楊氏，賜錢三萬貫，酒三十斛，米麥各百斛，編之屬籍，為皇從孫。」

translations.literal: Yichen may be granted the surname Yang, granted thirty thousand strings of cash, thirty hu of wine, one hundred hu each of rice and wheat, entered in the imperial clan register, and made an imperial clansman from the younger branch."
translations.idiomatic: Yichen shall be granted the surname Yang, thirty thousand strings of cash, thirty hu of wine, one hundred hu each of rice and wheat, enrollment in the imperial clan register, and the status of imperial clansman from the younger line."

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜陝州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Governor of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 義臣性謹厚，能馳射，有將領之才，由是上甚重之。

translations.literal: Yichen's nature was cautious and honest; he could ride and shoot and had the talent of a general, and therefore the emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen was cautious and steady, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and showed real commander's talent, so the emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥達頭可汗犯塞，以行軍總管率步騎三萬出白道，與賊遇，戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Afterwards, when Tujue Qaghan Tatou violated the border, as Campaign Governor-General he led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry out the White Road, encountered the enemy, fought, and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tardu Qaghan of the Turks raided the frontier, Yichen marched as campaign governor-general with thirty thousand horse and foot out the White Road, met the enemy in battle, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 明年，突厥又寇邊，雁門、馬邑多被其患。

translations.literal: The next year the Turks again raided the border, and Yanmen and Mayi largely suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Turks raided again, and Yanmen and Mayi suffered heavily.

sentences.zh: 義臣擊之，虜遂出塞，因而追之，至大斤山，與虜相遇。

translations.literal: Yichen struck them; the captives then went out of the border, and he pursued them to Dajin Mountain, where he encountered the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen attacked them; the raiders fled beyond the border, and he pursued them to Dajin Mountain, where he caught up with them.

sentences.zh: 時太平公史萬歲軍亦至，義臣與萬歲合軍擊虜，大破之，萬歲為楊素所陷而死，義臣功竟不錄。

translations.literal: At the time the army of Duke of Taiping Shi Wansui also arrived; Yichen and Wansui combined armies to strike the barbarians and routed them greatly. Wansui was framed by Yang Su and died, and Yichen's merit was ultimately not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wansui, Duke of Taiping, then arrived with his army; Yichen joined forces with him and won a great victory. Wansui was destroyed by Yang Su and died, and Yichen's achievements went unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，拜朔州總管，賜以禦甲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was appointed Governor-General of Shuozhou and granted imperial armor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Renshou era he became governor-general of Shuozhou and was granted imperial armor.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，漢王諒作亂并州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, the Prince of Han Liang rebelled at Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Prince Liang of Han rebelled in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時代州總管李景為漢王將喬鐘葵所圍，詔義臣救之。

translations.literal: At the time Governor-General of Daizhou Li Jing was besieged by the Han Wang's general Qiao Zhongkui; an edict ordered Yichen to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-general Li Jing of Daizhou was then besieged by Qiao Zhongkui, a general of Prince Liang; Yichen was ordered to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 義臣率馬步二萬，夜出西陘，遲明行數十裡。

translations.literal: Yichen led twenty thousand horse and foot, at night exited West Pass, and by dawn had marched several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen led twenty thousand horse and foot, stole out by night through West Pass, and by dawn had marched several tens of li.

sentences.zh: 鐘葵覘見義臣兵少，悉眾拒之。

translations.literal: Zhongkui observed and saw that Yichen's troops were few and gathered his entire force to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkui saw how few men Yichen had and massed his whole army to block him.

sentences.zh: 鐘葵亞將王拔驍勇，善用矛，射之者不能中，每以數騎陷陣。

translations.literal: Zhongkui's second-in-command Wang Ba was fierce and brave and skilled with the spear; those who shot at him could not hit him, and each time with several riders he charged the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkui's lieutenant Wang Ba was a fierce warrior with the spear; arrows could not bring him down, and again and again he broke the line with a handful of riders.

sentences.zh: 義臣患之，募能當拔者。

translations.literal: Yichen was troubled by this and recruited one who could match Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen was vexed by this and sought a man who could stand against Ba.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍楊思恩請當之。

translations.literal: Cavalry General Yang Si'en requested to take him on.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry general Yang Si'en volunteered to face him.

sentences.zh: 義臣見思恩氣貌雄勇，顧之曰：「壯士也！」

translations.literal: Yichen saw that Si'en's bearing was bold and fierce, turned to him and said: "A stalwart!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Si'en's bold and fierce mien, Yichen turned to him and said, "A true warrior!"

sentences.zh: 賜以卮酒。

translations.literal: He granted him a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: and gave him a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 思恩望見拔立於陣後，投觴於地，策馬赴之。

translations.literal: Si'en saw Ba standing at the rear of the formation, threw his cup to the ground, and whipped his horse toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Si'en spotted Ba at the rear of the enemy line, flung down his cup, and spurred straight at him.

sentences.zh: 再往不克，義臣複選騎士十余人從之。

translations.literal: Twice he went but could not overcome him; Yichen again selected more than ten mounted warriors to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he charged and failed; Yichen then chose more than ten mounted warriors to go with him.

sentences.zh: 思恩遂突擊，殺數人，直至拔麾下。

translations.literal: Si'en then charged in assault, killed several men, and went straight to beneath Ba's banner.
translations.idiomatic: Si'en then drove home his attack, cut down several men, and reached Ba's own standard.

sentences.zh: 短兵方接，所從騎士退，思恩為拔所殺。

translations.literal: At close quarters they had just joined battle when the mounted warriors who followed retreated, and Si'en was killed by Ba.
translations.idiomatic: They had just closed in hand to hand when the riders with him fell back, and Ba killed Si'en.

sentences.zh: 拔遂乘之，義臣軍北者十餘裡。

translations.literal: Ba then pressed the advantage, and Yichen's army retreated north more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Ba pressed the advantage, and Yichen's army fell back northward more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 於是購得思恩屍，義臣哭之甚慟，三軍莫不下泣。

translations.literal: Then they purchased Si'en's corpse; Yichen wept for him exceedingly, and all three armies none failed to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered Si'en's body at a price; Yichen mourned him bitterly, and the whole army wept.

sentences.zh: 所從騎士皆腰斬。

translations.literal: The mounted warriors who had followed were all cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: The riders who had retreated were all executed by waist-slicing.

sentences.zh: 義臣自以兵少，悉取軍中牛驢，得數千頭，複令兵數百人，人持一鼓，潛驅之澗穀間，出其不意。

translations.literal: Yichen himself, because his troops were few, took all the oxen and donkeys in the army, got several thousand head, and again ordered several hundred soldiers each holding one drum, secretly driving them through ravines and valleys to strike with surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his force was too small, Yichen gathered every ox and donkey in the army—several thousand head—and sent several hundred men, each with a drum, to drive them secretly through ravines and valleys for a surprise blow.

sentences.zh: 義臣晡後複與鐘葵軍戰，兵初合，命驅牛驢者疾進。

translations.literal: In the afternoon Yichen again fought Zhongkui's army; when the troops first joined battle he ordered those driving the oxen and donkeys to advance quickly.
translations.idiomatic: That afternoon Yichen engaged Zhongkui again; as the lines met he ordered the ox-and-donkey drivers to rush forward.

sentences.zh: 一時鳴鼓，塵埃張天，鐘葵軍不知，以為伏兵發，因而大潰，縱擊破之。

translations.literal: All at once the drums sounded, dust filled the sky, Zhongkui's army did not know what was happening, thought ambush troops had emerged, and therefore routed in great disorder; he released pursuit and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Drums burst out at once and dust blotted the sky; Zhongkui's men, thinking an ambush had sprung, broke and fled in panic, and Yichen chased them to complete rout.

sentences.zh: 以功進位上大將軍，賜物二千段，雜彩五百段，女妓十人，良馬二十匹。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced to Senior General-in-Chief and granted two thousand bolts of goods, five hundred bolts of mixed silks, ten female entertainers, and twenty fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted to senior general-in-chief and rewarded with two thousand bolts of goods, five hundred bolts of colored silks, ten female entertainers, and twenty fine horses.

sentences.zh: 尋授相州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後三歲，征為宗正卿。

translations.literal: Three years later he was summoned as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was recalled as director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉太僕卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，令義臣屯琵琶峽，連營八十裡，南接元壽，北連段文振，合圍渾主于覆袁川。

translations.literal: On campaign against Tuyuhun he ordered Yichen to encamp at Pipa Pass with connected camps for eighty li, south connecting with Yuan Shou and north connecting with Duan Wenzhen, jointly besieging the Tuyuhun ruler at Fuyuan River.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tuyuhun campaign Yichen was posted at Pipa Pass with camps stretching eighty li, linking south with Yuan Shou and north with Duan Wenzhen to surround the Tuyuhun ruler at the Fuyuan River.

sentences.zh: 其後複征遼東，以軍將指肅慎道。

translations.literal: Afterwards he again campaigned in Liaodong, and as army commander he directed operations on the Sushen route.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the Liaodong campaign again, commanding operations along the Sushen route.

sentences.zh: 至鴨綠水，與乙支文德戰，每為先鋒，一日七捷。

translations.literal: When he reached the Yalu River he fought with Eulji Mundeok; each time he served as vanguard, with seven victories in one day.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yalu River he battled Eulji Mundeok, leading the van again and again and winning seven engagements in a single day.

sentences.zh: 後與諸軍俱敗，竟坐免。

translations.literal: Later he suffered defeat together with the other armies, and in the end was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: He was later defeated along with the rest of the army and, in the end, stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 俄而復位。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 明年，以為軍副，與大將軍宇文述趣平壤。

translations.literal: The next year, he was made deputy to the army and, together with Grand General Yuwen Shu, marched toward Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed army deputy and, with Grand General Yuwen Shu, advanced on Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 至鴨綠水，會楊玄感作亂，班師，檢校趙郡太守。

translations.literal: When they reached the Yalu River, Yang Xuangan rose in rebellion; the army withdrew, and Yichen was made acting Grand Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: They had reached the Yalu when Yang Xuangan rebelled. The expedition was called off, and Yichen was assigned as acting Grand Administrator of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 妖賊向海公聚眾作亂，寇扶風、安定間，義臣奉詔擊平之。

translations.literal: The demonic bandit Xiang Haigong gathered a host and rebelled, raiding between Fufeng and Anding; Yichen received an edict and attacked, pacifying him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Xiang Haigong raised a force and harassed the region between Fufeng and Anding. Yichen was ordered to attack and put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 尋從帝複征遼東，進位左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he followed the emperor on another campaign against Liaodong and was promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon accompanied the emperor on another Liaodong campaign and was promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時渤海高士達，清河張金稱並相聚為盜，眾已數萬，攻陷郡縣。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Shida of Bohai and Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe had both banded together as bandits; their forces already numbered in the tens of thousands, and they had stormed commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Shida of Bohai and Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe had banded together as bandits. Their followers already numbered in the tens of thousands, and they were overrunning commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 帝遣將軍段達討之，不能克。

translations.literal: The emperor sent General Duan Da to attack them, but he could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent General Duan Da against them, but Duan could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 詔義臣率遼東還兵數萬擊之，大破士達，斬金稱。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yichen to lead several tens of thousands of troops returning from Liaodong to attack them; he routed Shida and beheaded Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen was ordered to lead the tens of thousands of troops returning from Liaodong against them. He crushed Gao Shida and killed Zhang Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 又收合降賊，入豆子<鹵亢>，討格謙，擒之，以狀聞奏。

translations.literal: He also gathered surrendered bandits, entered the Douzi foothills, attacked Ge Qian, captured him, and reported the circumstances in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He then reassembled surrendered rebels, marched into the Douzi foothills, attacked Ge Qian, captured him, and reported his success to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝惡其威名，遽追入朝，賊由是複盛。

translations.literal: The emperor resented his renown and hastily recalled him to court; the bandits therefore grew strong again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, resentful of his growing renown, abruptly recalled him to court, and the rebels flourished once more.

sentences.zh: 義臣以功進位光祿大夫，尋拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: For his merit Yichen was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and before long was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: For his victories Yichen was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and soon after appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office not long afterward.

sentences.zh: ○衛玄

translations.literal: ○ Wei Xuan
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuan

sentences.zh: 衛玄，字文升，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Wei Xuan, style name Wensheng, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuan, whose style name was Wensheng, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖悅，魏司農卿，父扌剽，侍中、左武衛大將軍，玄少有器識，周武帝在籓，引為記室。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yue was Minister of Agriculture under Wei; his father Bo was Palace Attendant and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard. Xuan in youth had talent and insight. When Emperor Wu of Zhou was still in his princely domain, he summoned him as a recorder.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yue had served Wei as Minister of Agriculture; his father Bo as Palace Attendant and Grand General of the Left Martial Guard. From youth Xuan showed ability and judgment. While Emperor Wu of Zhou was still a prince, he took Xuan on as a secretary.

sentences.zh: 遷給事上士，襲爵興勢公，食邑四千戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Clerk to the Emperor; he inherited the title Duke of Xingshi with a fief of four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Senior Clerk to the Emperor and inherited the dukedom of Xingshi, with a fief of four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 轉宣納下大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Spreading Instruction, Lower Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Spreading Instruction, Lower Rank.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，拜益州總管長史，賜以萬釘寶帶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally assumed charge of all affairs of state, Xuan was appointed Chief Clerk to the Governor-General of Yizhou and was granted a jeweled belt with ten thousand studs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took personal control of government, Xuan was appointed chief clerk to the Governor-General of Yizhou and was granted a jeweled belt studded with ten thousand nails.

sentences.zh: 稍遷開府儀同三司、太府中大夫，治內史事，仍領京兆尹，稱為強濟。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General with the Opening Office and ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, and Grand Master of the Grand Treasury, Middle Rank; he handled affairs of the Inner Scribe and concurrently served as Governor of Jingzhao, and was acclaimed as forceful and effective.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General with the Opening Office and ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, and Grand Master of the Grand Treasury, Middle Rank, managing the affairs of the Inner Scribe while also serving as Governor of Jingzhao. He was known for being vigorous and capable.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，以忤旨免官。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Xuan, he was dismissed from office for offending the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he lost his post for defying the throne.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，檢校熊州事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu served as Chancellor, Xuan was made acting supervisor of Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Xuan was put in charge of Xiong Prefecture on an acting basis.

sentences.zh: 和州蠻反，玄以行軍總管擊平之。

translations.literal: The barbarians of He Prefecture rebelled; Xuan, as Commander on Campaign, attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of He Prefecture rebelled, Xuan, as Commander on Campaign, attacked and subdued them.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，遷淮州總管，進封同軌郡公，坐事免。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Xuan was transferred to Governor-General of Huaizhou and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Tonggui Commandery, but was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu accepted the throne, Xuan was made Governor-General of Huaizhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Tonggui Commandery, but was later removed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜嵐州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Governor of Lan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was made Governor of Lan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會起長城之役，詔玄監督之。

translations.literal: When the project of building the Great Wall was undertaken, an edict ordered Xuan to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: When work began on the Great Wall, an edict put Xuan in charge of supervising the construction.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校朔州總管事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made acting supervisor of the Governor-General of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was assigned acting duties as Governor-General of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 後為衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: Later he became Vice Director of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Vice Director of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，山獠作亂，出為資州刺史以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Renshou era, the mountain Liao rebelled; he was sent out as Governor of Zi Prefecture to pacify and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Renshou era, when the mountain tribes rose in revolt, he was dispatched as Governor of Zi Prefecture to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 玄既到官，時獠攻圍大牢鎮，玄單騎造其營，謂群獠曰：「我是刺史，銜天子詔安養汝等，勿驚懼也。」

translations.literal: Once Xuan had taken up his post, the Liao were at that time besieging Dalao Fort. Xuan rode alone to their camp and said to the assembled Liao, "I am the Governor. I bear the Son of Heaven's edict to settle and nourish you—do not be alarmed or afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, Xuan found the tribes besieging Dalao Fort. He rode alone into their camp and told the assembled chiefs, "I am your governor. I come with the Son of Heaven's order to protect and provide for you. Have no fear.

sentences.zh: 諸賊莫敢動。

translations.literal: None of the bandits dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: None of the rebels dared move.

sentences.zh: 於是說以利害，渠帥感悅，解兵而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he explained the advantages and disadvantages to them; the chieftains were moved and pleased, laid down their arms, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke to them of gain and loss. The chieftains were won over, disbanded their forces, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 前後歸附者十餘萬口。

translations.literal: In all, more than a hundred thousand persons submitted and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end more than a hundred thousand people came over to his authority.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，賜縑二千匹，除遂州總管，仍令劍南安撫。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and granted him two thousand bolts of silk; he was appointed Governor-General of Suizhou and was still ordered to pacify Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and rewarded him with two thousand bolts of silk. Xuan was made Governor-General of Suizhou and charged with continuing the pacification of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，複征為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Xuan was again summoned and appointed Director of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Xuan was recalled and made Director of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 夷、獠攀戀，數百里不絕。

translations.literal: The Yi and Liao, clinging to him in attachment, stretched for several hundred li without break.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi and Liao clung to him in farewell, lining the road for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 玄曉之曰：「天子詔征，不可久住。」

translations.literal: Xuan explained to them, "The Son of Heaven has summoned me by edict—I cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan told them, "The Son of Heaven has summoned me. I cannot linger.

sentences.zh: 因與之訣，夷、獠各揮涕而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took leave of them; the Yi and Liao each waved tears and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He took his leave; the Yi and Liao wept as they saw him go.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 其後拜魏郡太守，尚書如故。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Administrator of Wei Commandery, while retaining his post as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Grand Administrator of Wei Commandery while keeping his ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 帝謂玄曰：「魏郡名都，衝要之所，民多奸宄，是用煩公。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Xuan, "Wei Commandery is a famous capital and a strategic crossroads; its people are full of rogues and evildoers—hence I trouble you with this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Xuan, "Wei Commandery is a celebrated seat and a vital crossroads. Its people are rife with schemers and criminals. That is why I must impose on you.

sentences.zh: 此郡去都，道裡非遠，宜數往來，詢謀朝政。」

translations.literal: This commandery is not far from the capital in distance; you should come and go frequently and consult on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery is not far from the capital. You should come and go often and keep me advised on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 賜物五百段而遣之。

translations.literal: He granted him five hundred bolts of goods and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him five hundred bolts of goods and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜右候衛大將軍，檢校左候衛事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand General of the Right Garrison Guard and made acting supervisor of the Left Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Grand General of the Right Garrison Guard and put in acting charge of the Left Garrison Guard as well.

sentences.zh: 大業八年，轉刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daye he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Daye he became Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，檢校右禦衛大將軍，率師出增地道。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign he was made acting Grand General of the Right Imperial Guard and led troops out through Zengdi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaodong campaign he served as acting Grand General of the Right Imperial Guard and led troops out through Zengdi Pass.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍多不利，玄獨全眾而還。

translations.literal: At that time most of the armies fared badly; Xuan alone brought his entire force back intact.
translations.idiomatic: While most of the army met with disaster, Xuan alone brought his force back intact.

sentences.zh: 拜金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 九年，車駕幸遼東，使玄與代王侑留守京師，拜為京兆內史，尚書如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when the imperial carriage went to Liaodong, the emperor had Xuan and Prince Dai You remain to guard the capital; Xuan was appointed Inner Scribe of Jingzhao, retaining his ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the emperor marched on Liaodong, he left Xuan and Prince Dai You to hold the capital. Xuan was appointed Inner Scribe of Jingzhao while keeping his ministerial title.

sentences.zh: 許以便宜從事，敕代王待以師傅之禮。

translations.literal: He was granted authority to act at his own discretion, and an edict ordered that Prince Dai treat him with the ceremony due a mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was authorized to act at his own discretion, and Prince Dai was instructed to treat him with the deference owed a teacher.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感圍逼東都，玄率步騎七萬援之。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan besieged and pressed the Eastern Capital, Xuan led seventy thousand infantry and cavalry to reinforce it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan laid siege to the Eastern Capital, Xuan led seventy thousand foot and horse to its relief.

sentences.zh: 至華陰，掘楊素塚，焚其骸骨，夷其塋域，示士卒以必死。

translations.literal: When he reached Huayin, he dug up Yang Su's tomb, burned his bones, leveled his burial ground, and thereby showed the troops that death was the only option.
translations.idiomatic: At Huayin he exhumed Yang Su's tomb, burned the bones, and razed the burial grounds—showing his soldiers they must fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 既出潼關，議者恐崤、函有伏兵，請於陝縣沿流東下，直趣河陽，以攻其背。

translations.literal: After passing out of Tong Pass, those in council feared an ambush in the Xiao and Han gorges and asked that he go down the river from Shaan County, heading straight for Heyang to strike the enemy's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Once through Tong Pass, his advisers feared an ambush in the Qin Mountains passes and urged him to follow the river east from Shaan County straight to Heyang and strike the rebels from behind.

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「以吾度之，此計非豎子所及。」

translations.literal: Xuan said, "By my reckoning, this plan is beyond what that worthless fellow could conceive.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "By my judgment, that plan is beyond what such a stripling could have devised.

sentences.zh: 於是鼓行而進。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: He marched forward at the beat of the drums.

sentences.zh: 既度函穀，卒如所量。

translations.literal: After crossing Hangu Pass, it turned out exactly as he had judged.
translations.idiomatic: After passing Hangu Pass, events unfolded exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 於是遣武賁郎將張峻為疑軍于南道，玄以大兵直趣城北。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Valiant Guard Lieutenant Zhang Jun with a decoy force on the southern route, while Xuan led the main army straight toward the north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Valiant Guard Lieutenant Zhang Jun with a diversionary force along the southern road, while he himself led the main army straight for the north of the city.

sentences.zh: 玄感逆拒之，且戰且行，屯軍金穀。

translations.literal: Xuangan met and resisted him, fighting as he moved, and encamped his army at Jingu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan marched out to meet him, fighting as he withdrew, and made camp at Jingu.

sentences.zh: 于軍中掃地而祭高祖曰：「刑部尚書、京兆內史臣衛文升，敢昭告于高祖文皇帝之靈：自皇家啟運，三十餘年，武功文德，漸被海外。

translations.literal: In the army he swept the ground and offered sacrifice to Gaozu, saying, "Minister of Justice and Inner Scribe of Jingzhao, your subject Wei Wensheng, ventures to declare to the spirit of Emperor Wen, founding emperor of Gaozu: Since the royal house opened its fortune, for more than thirty years martial achievement and civil virtue have gradually spread over the seas beyond.
translations.idiomatic: In camp he swept clean a plot of ground and offered sacrifice to Gaozu, saying, "Your subject Wei Wensheng, Minister of Justice and Inner Scribe of Jingzhao, declares before the spirit of Emperor Wen: Since the dynasty received the Mandate, more than thirty years have passed. Its martial might and civil virtue have spread even beyond the seas.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感孤負聖恩，躬為蛇豕，蜂飛蟻聚，犯我王略。

translations.literal: Yang Xuangan betrayed sagely grace, himself becoming a snake or swine; like bees flying and ants gathering, he has violated our royal frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan has betrayed imperial grace and turned serpent and pig himself. Swarming like bees and ants, he has violated the throne's dominion.

sentences.zh: 臣二世受恩，一心事主，董率熊羆，志梟凶逆。

translations.literal: Your subject has received favor through two reigns and serves his lord with a single heart; I lead bear and tiger forces, resolved to decapitate the wicked rebel.
translations.idiomatic: I have been favored through two reigns and serve my sovereign with undivided loyalty. I lead troops bold as bears and tigers, resolved to behead this villain.

sentences.zh: 若社稷靈長，宜令醜徒冰碎，如或大運去矣，幸使老臣先死。」

translations.literal: If the altars of state endure, may these vile rabble be shattered like ice; but if the great fate has already departed, let this old minister die first.
translations.idiomatic: If the altars of state endure, may these wretched rebels be shattered like ice. But if the dynasty's fortune has already turned, then let this old servant die first.

sentences.zh: 詞氣抑揚，三軍莫不涕咽。

translations.literal: His words rose and fell in cadence; throughout the three armies none failed to weep with choked throats.
translations.idiomatic: His words rang with passion; across the whole army men wept till they could barely speak.

sentences.zh: 時眾寡不敵，與賊頻戰不利，死傷大半。

translations.literal: At that time their numbers could not match the enemy's; they fought the bandits repeatedly without success, and more than half were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, they fought the rebels again and again without success. More than half the force was killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 玄感盡銳來攻，玄苦戰，賊稍卻，進屯北芒。

translations.literal: Xuangan brought all his picked troops to attack; Xuan fought bitterly, the bandits gradually fell back, and he advanced and encamped at Northern Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan threw in his best troops. Xuan fought desperately and slowly drove the rebels back, advancing to encamp at Northern Mang.

sentences.zh: 會宇文述、來護兒等援兵至，玄感懼而西遁。

translations.literal: When reinforcements under Yuwen Shu, Lai Huer, and others arrived, Xuangan grew afraid and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: When reinforcements under Yuwen Shu and Lai Huer arrived, Xuangan took fright and fled west.

sentences.zh: 玄遣通議大夫斛斯萬善、監門直閣龐玉前鋒追之，及於閿鄉，與宇文述等合擊破之。

translations.literal: Xuan sent Privy Counselor Husi Wanshan and Direct Attendant of the Gate Inspector Pang Yu with the vanguard in pursuit; they caught up at Wenxiang and, joining with Yuwen Shu and the others, combined their attack and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent Privy Counselor Husi Wanshan and Direct Attendant of the Gate Inspector Pang Yu in pursuit. They caught up at Wenxiang and, joining Yuwen Shu's force, broke the rebels completely.

sentences.zh: 車駕至高陽，征詣行在所。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Gaoyang, Xuan was summoned to the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Gaoyang, Xuan was summoned to the encampment.

sentences.zh: 帝勞之曰：「社稷之臣也。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled him, saying, "A pillar of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him: "You are a pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 使朕無西顧之憂。」

translations.literal: You have spared Us the worry of looking west.
translations.idiomatic: You have spared me all fear for the west.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「近者妖氛充斥，擾動關、河，文升率勵義勇，應機響赴，表裡奮擊，摧破凶醜，宜升榮命，式弘賞典。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict saying, "Recently demonic vapors have filled the land and disturbed the Pass and River regions. Wensheng has led and encouraged righteous volunteers, responded to the moment and rushed to the call, struck hard within and without, and crushed the wicked villains. It is fitting to raise his rank and title and magnify the canon of reward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Evil omens have lately filled the land and stirred turmoil in the Pass and Yellow River regions. Wensheng rallied loyal volunteers, answered the crisis at once, and struck the rebels within and without until they broke. Let his honors be raised and our rewards made plain.

sentences.zh: 可右光祿大夫。」

translations.literal: He is appointed Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 賜以良田、甲第，資物巨萬。

translations.literal: He was granted fine fields, a mansion of the first rank, and goods worth tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted fertile land, a fine mansion, and goods worth a fortune.

sentences.zh: 還鎮京師，帝謂之曰：「關右之任，一委於公。

translations.literal: Returning to guard the capital, the emperor said to him, "The charge of the region west of the Pass is wholly entrusted to you.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, the emperor told him, "The safety of the region west of the Pass rests entirely on you.

sentences.zh: 公安，社稷乃安；

translations.literal: When you are secure, the altars of state are secure;
translations.idiomatic: When you are secure, the realm is secure;

sentences.zh: 公危，社稷亦危。

translations.literal: when you are imperiled, the altars of state are also imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: when you are imperiled, the realm is imperiled as well.

sentences.zh: 出入須有兵衛，坐臥恆宜自牢，勇夫重閉，此其義也。

translations.literal: Going out and coming in you must have armed guards; sitting and lying down you should always keep yourself secure—the meaning of 'the brave man keeps double locks.'
translations.idiomatic: You must have armed guards whenever you go out, and never let down your guard even at rest. The saying runs that a brave man keeps his doors double-barred—and that is the idea.

sentences.zh: 今特給千兵，以充侍從。」

translations.literal: Now We specially grant you a thousand troops to serve as your escort.
translations.idiomatic: I hereby assign you a thousand soldiers as your personal guard.

sentences.zh: 賜以玉麟符。

translations.literal: He was granted the jade unicorn tally.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given the jade tally of command.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔玄安撫關中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict ordered Xuan to pacify and reassure Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was ordered to pacify Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊蜂起，百姓饑饉，玄竟不能救恤，而官方壞亂，貨賄公行。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose like swarming bees, the people suffered famine, Xuan ultimately could not relieve and succor them, and the officialdom fell into disorder with bribes openly traded.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed everywhere and the people starved, yet Xuan could not relieve them. Officialdom collapsed into chaos, and bribery ran unchecked.

sentences.zh: 玄自以年老，上表乞骸骨，帝使內史舍人封德彝馳諭之曰：「京師國本，王業所基，宗廟園陵所在，藉公耆舊，臥以鎮之。

translations.literal: Xuan, considering himself old, submitted a memorial requesting to retire; the emperor sent Palace Secretary Feng Deyi posthaste to instruct him, saying, "The capital is the root of the state, the foundation of the royal enterprise, where the ancestral temples and imperial tombs lie—I rely on your senior standing to hold it even from your couch.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling his age, Xuan asked to retire. The emperor sent Palace Secretary Feng Deyi posthaste with this message: "The capital is the foundation of the realm, the seat of our royal enterprise, where ancestral temples and imperial tombs stand. I depend on your stature and experience to hold it firm, even from your bed.

sentences.zh: 朕為國計，義無相許，故遣德彝口陳指意。」

translations.literal: For the sake of the state We cannot in duty grant your request, and therefore We send Deyi to convey Our intent in person.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of the state I cannot agree, and have sent Deyi to tell you so in person.

sentences.zh: 玄乃止。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan withdrew his request.

sentences.zh: 義師入關，自知不能守，憂懼稱疾，不知政事。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered the Pass, knowing he could not hold out, he grew anxious and afraid, claimed illness, and ceased to attend to affairs of government.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel army entered the Pass, knowing he could not hold the city, he grew anxious, pleaded illness, and abandoned all affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 城陷，歸於家。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 義甯中卒，時年七十七。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yining, at the age of seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Yining, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 子孝則，官至通事舍人、兵部承務郎，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoze rose to the posts of Communication Secretary and Assistant Clerk in the Ministry of War, and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoze rose to Communication Secretary and Assistant Clerk in the Ministry of War, but died young.

sentences.zh: ○劉權

translations.literal: ○ Liu Quan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan

sentences.zh: 劉權，字世略，彭城豐人也。

translations.literal: Liu Quan, style name Shilüe, was a native of Feng in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan, whose style name was Shilüe, came from Feng in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖軌，齊羅州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui was Governor of Luo Prefecture under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui had served Qi as Governor of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 權少有俠氣，重然諾，藏亡匿死，吏不敢過門。

translations.literal: Quan in youth had a chivalrous spirit and prized keeping his word; he hid fugitives and covered up for the condemned, and officials did not dare pass his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Quan had the temper of a knight-errant and prized his word above all. He sheltered fugitives and the condemned, and magistrates did not dare cross his threshold.

sentences.zh: 後更折節好學，動循法度。

translations.literal: Later he changed his ways, bent himself to study, and in conduct followed the law.
translations.idiomatic: Later he reformed himself, took up learning, and conducted himself by the law.

sentences.zh: 初為州主簿，仕齊，釋褐奉朝請、行台郎中。

translations.literal: At first he served as Chief Clerk of the prefecture; under Qi he entered service as a Responder at Court and Staff Officer of the Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a prefectural chief clerk. Under Qi he entered service as Responder at Court and Staff Officer of the Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及齊滅，周武帝以為假淮州刺史。

translations.literal: When Qi was destroyed, Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed him acting Governor of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi's fall, Emperor Wu of Zhou made him acting Governor of Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，以車騎將軍領鄉兵。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and put in charge of local militia.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Quan was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and given command of local militia.

sentences.zh: 後從晉王廣平陳，以功進授開府儀同三司，賜物三千段。

translations.literal: Later he followed Prince Jin in pacifying Chen; for his merit he was promoted and granted General with the Opening Office and ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, and was given three thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Prince Jin in the campaign to pacify Chen and, for his merits, was promoted to General with the Opening Office and ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, with a grant of three thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 宋國公賀若弼甚禮之。

translations.literal: Duke of Song, He Ruo Bi, treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Bi, Duke of Song, treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 開皇十二年，拜蘇州刺史，賜爵宗城縣公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaihuang he was appointed Governor of Su Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Zongcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Kaihuang he was made Governor of Su Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Zongcheng County.

sentences.zh: 于時江南初平，物情尚擾，權撫以恩信，甚得民和。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiangnan region had only just been pacified; public sentiment was still unsettled, but Quan soothed the people with kindness and trustworthiness and won their hearts thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: The south had only just been pacified and the people were still uneasy, but Quan won them over with kindness and trust until harmony prevailed.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜衛尉卿，進位銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Quan was appointed Minister of the Guards and advanced to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Quan was made Minister of the Guards and promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，從征吐谷渾，權率眾出伊吾道，與賊相遇，擊走之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, on the campaign against Tuyuhun, Quan led troops out by the Yiwu route, encountered the enemy, and struck them in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye, during the expedition against Tuyuhun, Quan led his forces along the Yiwu route, clashed with the enemy, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 逐北至青海，虜獲千餘口，乘勝至伏俟城。

translations.literal: Pursuing north to Qinghai, he captured captives numbering more than a thousand mouths, and riding victory reached Fuqi City.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them north as far as Qinghai, he took more than a thousand captives and pressed his advantage all the way to Fuqi City.

sentences.zh: 帝複令權過曼頭、赤水，置河源郡、積石鎮，大開屯田，留鎮西境。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Quan to pass Mantou and Chishui, establish Heyuan Commandery and Jishi Garrison, open garrison farming on a large scale, and remain to guard the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Quan through Mantou and Chishui to establish Heyuan Commandery and the Jishi garrison, launch large-scale military colonies, and stay on to guard the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 在邊五載，諸羌懷附，貢賦歲入，吐谷渾餘燼遠遁，道路無壅。

translations.literal: On the frontier for five years, the various Qiang came to attach themselves to him; tribute and levies entered yearly; the remaining embers of Tuyuhun fled far away; roads were without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: For five years on the frontier the Qiang tribes rallied to him, annual tribute flowed in, the surviving Tuyuhun bands fled into the distance, and the roads lay open.

sentences.zh: 征拜司農卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 加位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His rank was increased to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 尋為南海太守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he became Grand Administrator of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed grand administrator of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 行至鄱陽，會群盜起，不得進，詔令權召募討之。

translations.literal: When he reached Poyang, bandits rose in masses; he could not advance; an edict ordered Quan to recruit troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Poyang, widespread banditry broke out and he could not continue; the court ordered Quan to raise troops and put the rebels down.

sentences.zh: 權率兵與賊相遇，不與戰，先乘單舸詣賊營，說以利害。

translations.literal: Quan led troops and met the bandits; he did not engage them in battle, but first took a single boat to visit the bandit camp and expounded advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Quan marched out and encountered the rebels, but rather than fight he first took a lone boat to their camp and reasoned with them about the costs and consequences.

sentences.zh: 群賊感悅，一時降附，帝聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: The bandits as a group were moved and pleased and all at once submitted; the emperor heard of it and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were deeply moved and surrendered en masse; when the emperor heard of it, he praised Quan's achievement.

sentences.zh: 既至南海，甚有異政。

translations.literal: After he arrived at Nanhai, his governance was very exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Nanhai, he distinguished himself with remarkable administration.

sentences.zh: 數歲，遇盜賊群起，數來攻郡，豪帥多願推權為首，權竟盡力固守以拒之。

translations.literal: Several years later, encountering bandits rising in groups, they repeatedly came to attack the commandery; local magnates mostly wished to make Quan their leader, but Quan in the end exerted his full strength in firm defense to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: After a few years bandits rose in force and repeatedly attacked the commandery; many local leaders wanted to make Quan their head, but he threw all his energy into holding the city against them.

sentences.zh: 子世徹又密遣人齎書詣權，稱四方擾亂，英雄並起，時不可失，諷令舉兵。

translations.literal: His son Shiche again secretly sent a man bearing a letter to Quan, declaring that the four quarters were in disorder, heroes were rising together, the time must not be lost, and hinting that he should raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiche also secretly sent an envoy with a letter urging that with turmoil everywhere and heroes rising on every side, the moment must not be missed—and suggesting that Quan should take up arms.

sentences.zh: 權召集佐僚，對斬其使，竟無異圖，守之以死。

translations.literal: Quan summoned his aides and subordinates, beheaded the envoy before them, ultimately harbored no other design, and defended to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Quan assembled his staff, executed the messenger before them all, never wavered in his loyalty, and vowed to hold the city unto death.

sentences.zh: 卒官，時年七十。

translations.literal: He died in office; he was seventy years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 世徹倜儻不羈，頗為時人所許。

translations.literal: Shiche was free-spirited and unrestrained, and was rather praised by people of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Shiche was daring and unrestrained, and won considerable admiration among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 大業末，群雄並起，世徹所至之處，輒為所忌，多拘禁之，後竟為兗州賊帥徐圓朗所殺。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, competing lords rose together; wherever Shiche went he was at once envied, often detained, and in the end was killed by Xu Yuanlang, bandit chief of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Daye, as rival warlords rose on every side, Shiche was resented wherever he went, often imprisoned, and was eventually killed by Xu Yuanlang, a bandit chieftain in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 權從父烈，字子將，美容儀，有器局，官至鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: Quan's paternal uncle Lie, style name Zijiang, had handsome bearing and measure of capacity, and reached the office of Colonel Who Displays Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's uncle Lie, whose style name was Zijiang, was handsome in appearance and broad in outlook, and rose to colonel who displays majesty.

sentences.zh: 有子德威，知名於世。

translations.literal: He had a son Dewei, known to the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Dewei, who became well known in his own day.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：子蓋雅有幹局，質性嚴敏，見義而勇，臨機能斷，保全都邑，勤亦懋哉！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Zigai elegantly possessed capacity and decisiveness; his nature was stern and keen; seeing righteousness he was brave; facing opportunity he could decide; he preserved entire cities and towns—how earnest was his diligence!
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Zigai had true administrative talent, a stern and sharp temperament, courage when justice called for it, and decisive judgment in the moment; in preserving cities and towns his diligence was truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 楊諒干紀，史祥著獨克之效，群盜侵擾，義臣致三捷之功，此皆名重當年，聲流後葉者也。

translations.literal: When Yang Liang violated the law of the age, Shi Xiang displayed the effect of sole conquest; when bandits in groups harassed, Yichen achieved the merit of three victories—these all bore heavy names in their own year and their fame flows to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Liang violated imperial order, Shi Xiang won a victory all on his own; when bandits ravaged the land, Yichen scored three triumphs—these men were celebrated in their own time and their fame survives in later ages.

sentences.zh: 元壽彈奏行本，有意存夫名教，然其計功稱伐，猶居義臣之後，端揆之贈，不已優乎？

translations.literal: Yuan Shou impeached Xingben, with intent to preserve name and teaching; yet in reckoning achievement and proclaiming merit he still stood behind Yichen—is the gift of chief counselor not already too generous?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shou's impeachment of Liu Xingben was meant to uphold moral propriety, yet measured by martial achievement he still ranked below Yichen—was the grant of chief counselor not rather too lavish?

sentences.zh: 文升東都解圍，頗亦宣力，西京居守，政以賄成，鄙哉鄙哉，夫何足數！

translations.literal: Wensheng relieved the siege of the Eastern Capital and also fairly spread his strength; guarding the Western Capital, his government was achieved through bribes—base! base! How is he worth counting!
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng did exert himself in breaking the siege of the Eastern Capital, but while holding the Western Capital his rule was built on bribery—contemptible, contemptible; he scarcely merits mention at all!

sentences.zh: 劉權淮楚舊族，早著雄名，屬擾攘之辰，居尉佗之地，遂能拒子邪計，無所覬覦，雖謝勤王之謀，足為守節之士矣。

translations.literal: Liu Quan was an old clan of Huai and Chu, early showing a heroic name; in a time belonging to turmoil, dwelling in the land of Zhao Tuo, he was thus able to reject his son's wicked scheme, without any coveting; although he declined the plan to aid the throne, he is enough to be a man who holds to integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan came from an old Huai-Chu family and had won martial renown early on; in those turbulent years, holding a post in the far south where Zhao Tuo once ruled, he rejected his son's sedition and harbored no ambition of his own; though he never marched to rescue the throne, he may still be counted among men who kept their integrity.
